providers.name: Meisterwerk
providers.description: Meisterwerk is a modular all-in-one SaaS platform for German-speaking (DACH) trades and craft businesses (Handwerk), built by MEISTERWERK APP GmbH in Berlin. It gives small and medium craft firms (1-50 employees) a single operating system for job and resource scheduling (Einsatzplanung), a native mobile app for iOS, Android and Windows, chronological job documentation with photos and chat, quoting and invoicing with e-invoice support, EU-compliant mobile time tracking with GPS, digital forms and signatures, absence/holiday planning, and configurable workflows. AI features (planning assistant, speech-to-text documentation and time entry, and the standalone "Frag Maxi" phone assistant) are built in. It integrates with lexoffice, sevdesk, bexio and orgaMAX accounting software; a public open interface (Offene Schnittstelle) is announced but not yet publicly documented. Over 8,000 active users; data is hosted on servers in Germany and the platform is GDPR (DSGVO) compliant.

providers.name: Buildvision
providers.description: BuildVision is an AI bid-management and equipment-procurement platform for the construction industry. It monitors email inboxes and construction plan rooms for incoming bids, extracts equipment specifications from construction documents, matches them against a company's line card, and drafts quotes with automatic conflict detection and RFI generation. Products span bid triage automation, a "spec memory" of historical engineer data, equipment quoting, and channel intelligence for OEMs. BuildVision integrates with Microsoft Outlook and BuildingConnected and offers direct API / browser-agent integration to selection software by request, but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from BuildVision's public surface.

providers.name: Boxabl
providers.description: BOXABL Inc. is a Las Vegas, Nevada manufacturer of factory-built, foldable homes, founded in 2017 and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker BXBL. Its homes are assembled on a production line in a climate-controlled factory rather than on site, then folded to 8.5 by 20 feet for shipment by truck, rail, sea or air and unfolded on the pad in about two hours. The Casita is the current production model, sold as a studio, one-bedroom and two-bedroom in unit-only or turnkey configurations, with a Baby Box travel trailer and a multi-unit Developer Series catalog alongside it. BOXABL publishes no public API, developer portal or machine-readable API contract; its machine-readable surface is an agent-facing llms.txt, a permissive AI-crawler robots.txt, and an RFC 9116 security.txt pointing at a real responsible-disclosure and bug bounty policy.

providers.name: Planera
providers.description: Planera is a modern construction scheduling platform for builders and general contractors, purpose-built around the Critical Path Method (CPM). It lets teams build, manage, and optimize project schedules through a visual, collaborative interface with drag-and-drop editing, a digital whiteboard (Canvas), Gantt views, DCMA quality checks, resource planning, and an AI scheduling assistant (Manny) for scenario analysis and risk identification. Planera spans pursuits, preconstruction, operations, and enterprise portfolio management, offers an iPad field app, and integrates with Procore, Autodesk, Primavera P6, and Microsoft Project. The company is SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 certified and is backed by Sierra Ventures.

providers.name: Lennar
providers.description: Lennar Corporation is a Fortune 500 company and one of the leading homebuilders of new homes for sale in the United States. Lennar operates an internal Azure-hosted API Management developer portal where Lennar developers and partners discover and consume Lennar Corporation APIs. Public OpenAPI artifacts have not been observed; access generally requires sign-in and partner approval.

providers.name: Graneet
providers.description: Graneet is a French vertical-SaaS ERP for the construction and public-works (BTP) sector, built for small and mid-sized contractors (roughly EUR 2M to 100M in revenue) to protect project profitability from the office to the job site. It unifies cost estimating and quotations, progress (situation) invoicing, purchase and supplier-invoice management, project planning and labor tracking, cash and bank reconciliation, and real-time margin dashboards, with a companion mobile app and prebuilt integrations to accounting tools such as Sage 100 and Pennylane. The product is delivered as a cloud application (app.graneet.com) backed by internal Main, BFF, and Quotation APIs; there is no public developer API or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Motif
providers.description: Motif is an AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) software company building an intelligent, browser-based workspace for building design. Founded in 2023 by former Autodesk leaders Amar Hanspal and Brian Mathews, Motif unifies sheet review, live 3D streaming, AI-assisted visual exploration, and real-time collaboration in a single cloud platform that bridges 2D and 3D workflows as a step toward making Building Information Modeling (BIM) a practical reality. The company has raised $46M led by Redpoint Ventures (seed) and Alphabet's CapitalG (Series A), and was named to Forbes' 2025 Next Billion-Dollar Startups list. Motif is a collaboration SaaS product for design and construction teams; it publishes product learning docs and a help center but does not yet expose a public developer API — a plugin/API surface is part of its stated long-term strategy.

providers.name: OnStation
providers.description: OnStation is a digital stationing platform for road and highway construction projects, replacing paper station logs and manual chaining with GPS-based field documentation. Its iOS and Android mobile app lets crews, inspectors, and project managers identify exact station locations, drop and share flags, capture timestamped photos and notes, and complete forms in the field without extra hardware. A cloud Data Portal aggregates that field documentation into searchable, exportable DOT-ready reports for compliance and dispute resolution, while Active Worksite alerts drivers through Waze and OEM systems when crews are working. OnStation offers pre-built integrations with construction and survey systems including HCSS HeavyJob, Trimble and Bad Elf GNSS receivers, TransTech density gauges, FleetWatcher e-ticketing, and ESRI GIS, but does not currently publish a public developer API. Backed by Insight Partners and Techstars.

providers.name: Lessen
providers.description: Lessen is a Scottsdale, Arizona based property services and facilities management technology company that connects commercial and residential property owners and managers with a nationwide network of vetted service providers for repairs, maintenance, turns, make-readies and capital projects. The company operates a technology platform stack — One by Lessen for work-order, vendor-sourcing and invoicing workflow, Lessen 360 for multifamily maintenance, Lessen Pro for affiliate contractors, Aiden for AI-assisted work-order creation, and the Lessen Marketplace for procurement — supported by mobile apps for tenants, property managers and vendors. Lessen serves retail, financial services, healthcare, food service, industrial, hospitality and education properties alongside single-family and multifamily residential portfolios. Lessen acquired SMS Assist in 2023 and is backed by Fifth Wall and General Catalyst. Lessen publishes no public developer portal, API reference or OpenAPI definition; its named platform integrations are delivered as private partner connections rather than a self-serve API program.

providers.name: plancraft
providers.description: plancraft is a German cloud-based business management software for craftspeople and trades businesses (Handwerk). It digitizes administrative workflows end to end — quote and estimate creation, project planning, time tracking, on-site documentation, material and labor costing, and invoicing — inside one integrated platform aimed at small and mid-sized construction and trade companies. plancraft supports DATEV export for tax/accounting workflows and DATANORM and GAEB catalog imports for material data and tender processing. It is a venture-backed SaaS company (portfolio company of Creandum). As of this enrichment pass plancraft publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface — integrations are delivered as prebuilt connectors and standardized file-format import/export.

providers.name: Contractor Foreman
providers.description: Contractor Foreman is all-in-one construction management software for contractors - estimates, invoicing, scheduling, time cards, daily logs, change orders, and job costing - used by contractors in more than 75 countries. There is no self-serve public developer API or public API reference; the company's dedicated API subdomain (api.contractorforeman.net) displays only a "Coming soon" placeholder as of this review. The one confirmed API capability is a private, account-scoped API key (generated under Settings > Integration > Zapier) that powers Contractor Foreman's official Zapier app, exposing Customer and Lead create/archive/delete triggers and actions plus a File Uploaded trigger. That key and its underlying endpoints are not documented or published for direct third-party use outside the Zapier integration; broader third-party connectivity otherwise runs through native integrations (QuickBooks, Gusto, Google Calendar/Outlook, Stripe, Angi Leads, CompanyCam, MS Project, SweetPay) and Zapier/webhook automation rather than an open API.

providers.name: Roofr
providers.description: Roofr is an all-in-one roofing software and CRM built for roofing contractors, bundling aerial roof measurement reports, an instant online estimator, digital proposals with e-signature, integrated payments, material ordering, a job calendar, and pipeline/CRM tooling into one platform to help roofers win, run, and close jobs. Roofr does not publish a public developer API or self-serve documentation: the only API key it issues (under Settings and Integrations) exists to connect Roofr to Zapier, and any broader programmatic access is sales-gated behind a demo. Automation for external systems is delivered primarily through Zapier triggers (new Instant Estimator lead, proposal signed, proposal marked lost) rather than a documented REST API. Roofr is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital.

providers.name: Visibly
providers.description: Visibly is a UK-based workforce compliance management platform that helps enterprises with large, distributed and subcontracted workforces automate their HSEQ (health, safety, environment and quality) obligations. It centralizes worker onboarding, competency and certification tracking, real-time compliance monitoring and alerts, audit and project reporting, and safety broadcast communications, with integrations into existing HR, ERP, LMS and SharePoint systems and mobile-first workflows for field workers. It is used across construction, manufacturing, FMCG, energy, public services, infrastructure and logistics by organizations including Network Rail, National Grid, EDF, Scottish Power, NHS and Danone. Backed by Creandum and Seedcamp.

providers.name: Block Renovation
providers.description: Block Renovation is a home renovation and construction platform that connects homeowners with vetted, local contractors and provides free design, cost-estimation, and project-planning tools for kitchen and bathroom remodels, home additions, basement renovations, ADUs, new construction, and commercial projects. It operates across all 50 US states and layers on a protection program covering price assurance, progress-based payments, a workmanship warranty, and dedicated Project Planner support. Backed by Obvious Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund, it was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; as of this enrichment pass Block Renovation publishes a consumer-facing marketplace but no public developer API, documentation, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Datumate
providers.description: Datumate is a construction technology company whose cloud-native SaaS platform, DatuBIM, turns drone imagery, laser-scanning, and site data into real-time progress tracking, deviation detection, automated reporting, and actionable analytics for heavy civil infrastructure projects. It serves asset owners, general contractors, and engineering and consulting firms across roads, highways, rail, bridges, and earthworks, giving multi-site visibility from design validation through construction to final inspection. The company reports 125+ active customers, thousands of managed sites, and tens of thousands of processed drone flights. Datumate has Israeli engineering roots (Technion) with leadership based in Miami, Florida, and is backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Pillar
providers.description: Pillar is an Italian construction-technology company, founded in 2025 and headquartered in Milan, building what it calls the operating system for the construction industry (il sistema operativo per l'edilizia). Its cloud platform unifies the back office of building firms (imprese edili) — invoicing (fatturazione), cash-flow management (flussi di cassa), bank reconciliation, quotes and estimates (preventivi), procurement, job and project cost control (gestione commessa), and delivery notes and site work reports (DDT e rapportini) — alongside on-site safety (Pillar Sicurezza) and an AI layer (Pillar AI) that automates data entry in real time, including inputs captured from the job site over WhatsApp. Pillar is backed by Earlybird Venture Capital and today reaches customers through a book-a-demo model rather than a public self-serve signup or a developer-facing API; no public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Sketchdeck.ai
providers.description: SketchDeck.ai is a B2B SaaS company whose flagship product, LIFT, is AI-powered material takeoff and counting software for the structural steel fabrication and erection industry. LIFT analyzes uploaded blueprints and shop drawings to automatically extract quantities and generate Bills of Materials, with claimed 95-99% accuracy and up to an 80% reduction in takeoff time so estimators can complete bids in minutes rather than hours or days. The platform adds revision management and exports data to industry estimating programs; the company reports more than $25 billion in projects bid through LIFT to date. SketchDeck.ai is a Techstars-backed startup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and demo-request website only - there is no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification surface to catalog.

providers.name: FYLD
providers.description: FYLD is an AI-native frontline intelligence platform for the global critical-infrastructure sector, turning field-operations data into real-time, structured intelligence for utilities, energy, and heavy-civils operators. Its products include the FYLD Platform for work execution, FYLD Control Room for remote supervision, and FYLD ShowMe for customer self-service reporting, serving managers, fieldworkers, contractors, and civil engineers via web and mobile (iOS and Android) apps. FYLD is a Partech portfolio company. As of this profile FYLD publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; integration is delivered through partnerships such as Procore, and this record captures its public identity, security, and trust surface.

providers.name: Equipmentwatch
providers.description: EquipmentWatch (a Fusable brand) provides construction and equipment data APIs that deliver rental rates, ownership costs, market values, and specifications for heavy equipment. Their data is used by contractors, equipment dealers, rental houses, and insurance professionals to make informed decisions about equipment valuation, procurement, and rental.

providers.name: IronPlanet
providers.description: IronPlanet is an online marketplace for buying and selling used heavy construction equipment and trucks across categories including construction, trucks, agriculture, mining, forestry, and oil and gas. The platform offers online auctions, buy-now listings, make-an-offer, sealed auctions, and on-site auctions, with detailed third-party inspection reports backed by its IronClad Assurance certification program. IronPlanet operates regional marketplaces for North America, Europe/Middle East, and Asia-Pacific and is part of the Ritchie Bros. (RB Global) family of businesses. This company was surfaced as a portfolio company of accel and kleiner-perkins and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: JSW One
providers.description: JSW One Platforms is the digital B2B arm of India's JSW Group, operating a full-stack e-commerce and services platform for the country's manufacturing and construction MSMEs. It runs four connected businesses on one technology stack: JSW One Commerce (jswonemsme.com), a multi-brand marketplace for TMT bars, mild/hot-rolled/cold-rolled and structural steel, coated steel, wire rods, cement and bitumen sourced from certified mills; JSW One Homes (jswonehomes.com), a turnkey home-construction service with digital project tracking across fifteen Indian cities; JSW One Finance, the NBFC arm providing digital credit lines, channel financing and invoice factoring to MSMEs and retailers; and private brands JSW One TMT and One Helix. The platform reported FY25 gross merchandise value of INR 12,567 crore across more than 84,000 registered MSMEs, and raised INR 575 crore in a 2025 round led by the State Bank of India. JSW One publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its customer-facing surfaces are the web marketplace and the JSW One MSME mobile apps. It does publish a maintained llms.txt on both of its consumer properties, plus an explicit AI/LLM bot-access policy on JSW One Homes.

providers.name: Comstruct
providers.description: Comstruct is a Munich-based construction technology company that provides AI-powered agents to automate the procurement of construction materials. Its platform runs the full procurement workflow from the bill of materials (Leistungsverzeichnis) through supplier inquiry, offer comparison, contract negotiation, digital delivery notes, AI-based invoice verification, and sustainability reporting. Customers include HOCHTIEF, Implenia, Marti, and Leonhard Weiss. Comstruct is backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of enrichment the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or OpenAPI definition; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network from its public web presence.

providers.name: Construction Monitor
providers.description: Construction Monitor aggregates building-permit data from county and municipal sources nationwide and resells it as construction leads, contractor intelligence, and historical permit research. Programmatic access is offered through a REST + JSON API backed by Elasticsearch and a weekly data-dump option delivered over secure FTP. Both channels are account-managed; partners receive credentials and a documented endpoint contract directly from Construction Monitor.

providers.name: Parspec
providers.description: Parspec is an AI-native platform for electrical, lighting, and MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) distributors and manufacturer rep agencies in the construction supply chain. It consolidates fragmented, manual workflows into one system covering quoting for complex projects, automated submittal and O&M document creation, project management (orders, fulfillment, billing), and sales management, with ERP integrations (Epicor Eclipse, Epicor Prophet 21, SAP). Parspec is SOC 2 Type II attested and markets itself to help distributors and rep agencies bid more, win more, and improve profitability. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Abodu
providers.description: Abodu designs, manufactures, and installs prefabricated accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and backyard homes across California. It offers state-approved plans with fixed all-in pricing and installation as fast as one day, spanning seven models from the 385 sq ft Abodu Studio to the 1,195 sq ft Abodu Three+, plus an Abodu Office. The homes target homeowners seeking rental income, aging-in-place, home offices, and guest houses, as well as multifamily operators, and feature fire-resistant construction with an optional Net Zero solar package. Abodu is a Norwest Venture Partners portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Imerso
providers.description: Imerso is a construction management and quality-control software company that connects the onsite as-built reality to BIM models. Using 3D laser scanning (including a free Imerso Capture mobile app for Leica BLK360 scanners) and in-house AI models, its Site Checker automatically compares the built status of a jobsite against BIM plan specifications, surfacing deviations, progress tracking, and as-built data grouped by traffic-light categories. The platform targets general contractors and BIM teams for automated site supervision, progress reporting, and issue detection, and promotes 100% open data with direct integrations into tools such as Autodesk Construction Cloud. Imerso is a 500 Global portfolio company. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface has been found; this profile is maintained as a company record.

providers.name: Dusty Robotics
providers.description: Dusty Robotics is a construction-technology company building automated layout robotics for the building trades. Its flagship product, the FieldPrinter, is a mobile robot that prints digital BIM models and design drawings directly onto the jobsite floor at full scale, laying out walls, penetrations, and other design intent so field teams build to plan with far less manual measurement and rework. The FieldPrinter platform ingests drawings from tools like Autodesk Revit and AutoCAD via native plugins, translating the digital model into precise physical markings on the deck. Dusty Robotics is headquartered in Mountain View, California and is backed by investors including Canaan Partners. The company does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its published surfaces are the product site, a partner program, a support center, and the Dusty Academy training resource.

providers.name: SiteAware
providers.description: SiteAware is the construction industry's first AI-powered Digital Construction Verification and Quality Management Platform for buildings. It verifies every installed element and flags real-time deviations across structure, envelope, and interior construction, giving field teams and business executives actionable data and analytics to catch issues before they lead to expensive rework. SiteAware is a portfolio company of Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Tailorbird
providers.description: Tailorbird is a CapEx orchestration platform for the multifamily real estate industry, replacing spreadsheet-based capital planning with AI-generated property intelligence. The platform produces unit-level as-builts, takeoffs, and interior models, runs renovation ROI and five-year capital plans, and tracks spend and budget variance in real time across apartment portfolios. Tailorbird ingests PCAs and property documents, integrates with major property-management ERPs including Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, and MRI via custom APIs and ELTs, and maintains SOC 2 Type II compliance. Founded in 2020 and based in Princeton, New Jersey, it serves 28 of the NMHC Top 50 operators and manages more than $2B in annual CapEx across over one million mapped units. It is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company.

providers.name: Housable
providers.description: Housable is a California-focused proptech company that helps rental-property owners and operators develop Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) as a portfolio value-add strategy. Its platform manages ADU projects end to end — from concept and financial feasibility analysis through design, permitting, bidding, construction, and lease-up — and lets operators run many parallel developments across their properties at once, converting underused spaces such as leasing offices, garages, and parking areas into new rental units alongside ground-up ADU construction. Housable is an early-stage startup backed by Kindred Ventures and other seed investors. It is catalogued in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Sankun
providers.description: Sankun (산군) is a South Korean construction-industry big data platform based in Seoul that aggregates and sells access to eight integrated construction databases covering roughly 280,000 construction companies, some 820,000 project sites, government e-procurement bids, contract awards, professional reputation reviews, and construction news. Alongside its web application and a construction sales CRM (Sankun Sales), the company markets a Sankun API (data.sankun.com) for programmatic access to its construction data, though public developer documentation is gated behind sales and login. Sankun is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: Hitachi Construction Machinery
providers.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery provides operational data about machines and equipment on construction sites through the Telematics API, which complies with the ISO 15143-3 (AEMP 2.0) standard. The API enables higher efficiency, productivity, and safety while reducing life cycle costs.

providers.name: Foresight
providers.description: Foresight is a predictive project-delivery platform for complex construction and infrastructure megaprojects, with a particular focus on data centers, government, and critical infrastructure. Founded by Dr. Atif Ansar and Igor Shifrin (Oxford) and headquartered in London, it layers on top of existing scheduling tools such as Microsoft Project and Excel to turn raw schedule data into forecasts, risk assessment, delay prediction, and portfolio-wide project assurance. The company reports managing $100B+ in mission-critical projects and is backed by Creandum and Macquarie Capital. Foresight is delivered as a SaaS web application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Qbiq
providers.description: Qbiq is an AI-powered space planning and architectural visualization platform for real estate. It lets brokers, architects, developers, and space planners generate optimized 2D floor plans, photorealistic 3D renderings, virtual tours, Revit/CAD models, and quantity takeoffs from an uploaded space plan (CAD, PDF, or JPEG) in minutes. Qbiq automates test-fits and layout optimization for offices and commercial real estate, comparing multiple design options against program requirements. The company is backed by Insight Partners and was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC portfolio. As of this enrichment pass Qbiq operates a hosted web application (plan.qbiq.ai) and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Basebuild
providers.description: Basebuild Labs, Inc. builds Beams, an AI project manager for construction and real estate teams. The product automatically transcribes project meetings, tracks decisions and action items, and assembles a searchable knowledge base from those discussions, capturing information without requiring a bot to join the call. It is aimed at giving construction and real estate project teams real-time visibility and control over teams, projects, budgets, and finances. Basebuild is an early-stage Canaan Partners portfolio company based in Santa Monica, California, and this API Evangelist profile tracks its public-facing surface. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and a product login only, with no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, or documentation surface to catalog.

providers.name: Duranta
providers.description: Duranta Labs is an applied AI laboratory building geospatial and computer-vision technology to understand the physical world. Its foundation vision model, Aidan, generates accurate, current 4D digital twins from optical imagery. That model powers a Landscapers solution that lets professionals measure, design, and bid any property directly from imagery without a site visit, a general-purpose World Model for spatial intelligence, and a forthcoming AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) product that turns an address into a precise digital model. Duranta is backed by Fifth Wall.

providers.name: Foundation Building Materials
providers.description: Foundation Building Materials (FBM) is a leading North American distributor of interior building products — drywall, steel framing, acoustic ceilings, insulation, and complementary construction supplies — serving commercial and residential contractors across the United States and Canada. Headquartered in Santa Ana, California, FBM operates a national branch network and a unified customer ordering platform at myfbm.com (consolidating the legacy fbmsales.com, MyRIS, and MyFBM portals) along with iOS/Android mobile apps for contractors. In April 2025, FBM acquired KCG/Rew Materials, adding 800 employees and 45 distribution branches across 23 states. In August 2025, Lowe's announced an agreement to acquire FBM. Brand families operating under FBM include FBM, RIS, Pacific Source, and Unified Door. FBM does not currently expose any public developer APIs, OpenAPI documentation, partner integration program, SDK, or GitHub organization — its digital surface is limited to buyer-facing e-commerce (search, ordering, order tracking, quick-order PDF/photo ingestion via "Quick Order Entry") rather than a developer/integration product.

providers.name: PlanSwift
providers.description: PlanSwift is Windows desktop takeoff and estimating software for construction estimators - turning digital plans (PDF/image/CAD) into measurable, countable, exportable material takeoffs and estimates across trades like roofing, concrete, earthwork, flooring, and electrical. PlanSwift is owned by ConstructConnect. IMPORTANT - PlanSwift does NOT publish a public web/REST API. Its developer surface is a desktop extensibility SDK embedded in the Windows application - OLE Automation (COM), an internal scripting engine, and a plugin/starter-pack model - exposed through a password-gated "Under-The-Hood" (U-T-H) tab enabled by contacting ConstructConnect (takeoff@constructconnect.com). The public SDK examples on GitHub target PlanSwift9 and are written in Pascal (2008) and Visual Basic (2010). There is no documented HTTPS base URL, no API keys/OAuth token surface, and no web endpoints to model - this entry is an honest stub reflecting a desktop-plugin/COM SDK, not a web API.

providers.name: CoConstruct
providers.description: CoConstruct is a residential construction management software platform originally founded in 2005 in Charlottesville, Virginia by Donny Wyatt to help custom home builders and remodelers manage projects, budgets, selections, client communications, scheduling, and financial workflows in a single web and mobile application. The product served thousands of custom builders across the United States and was paired with CBUSA, a homebuilder group purchasing organization CoConstruct previously acquired. On February 24, 2021, CoConstruct was acquired by Buildertrend of Omaha, Nebraska, with growth funding from Bain Capital Tech Opportunities, HGGC, and Serent Capital, creating a combined company serving 23,000+ clients, 1.1M+ users, and $200B+ in annual construction project value. By 2022 Buildertrend had merged the two products into a single unified Buildertrend platform and migrated CoConstruct customers off the legacy product. CoConstruct historically operated a developer portal at developer.coconstruct.com exposing APIs for project, financial, and scheduling data, but as of the merger CoConstruct has paused new API development — "we are not establishing new API endpoints or connecting additional users to existing endpoints" — and the developer portal now redirects to a static notice page. Existing API connections are reportedly maintained but no public OpenAPI specification, SDK, or open-source release is published. Net-new integration work is directed to Buildertrend's own platform and partner program.

providers.name: Exodigo
providers.description: Exodigo is a subsurface intelligence company that maps what is underground and above ground without digging. Founded in 2021 by former Israeli intelligence officers and headquartered in the San Francisco Bay Area, it fuses ground-penetrating radar, electromagnetic (TDEM/FDEM), magnetic gradiometry and electrical sensing with GPS-RTK positioning, then processes the combined signal with AI to produce geolocated 3D maps of buried utilities, foundations and geotechnical conditions. Products span ExoInfo remote data intelligence (AI compilation of public records, engineering documents and imagery), on-site reality capture, AI engineering and digitization, and utility relocation services. Deliverables are handed to customers as GIS and CAD artifacts (Esri ArcGIS, AutoCAD, BIM) and through a client portal rather than a public developer API — as of this profiling pass Exodigo publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK or MCP server. Customers include LA Metro, Caltrans, National Grid, VINCI Construction and state DOTs.

providers.name: Jones
providers.description: Jones is a full-service SaaS platform purpose-built for insurance compliance in construction and commercial real estate, unifying Certificate of Insurance (COI) collection, deep insurance auditing, workflow automation, and a licensed brokerage in one platform. It pairs hundreds of insurance specialists with AI agents to review COIs and policies at enterprise scale, and is used by general contractors, construction managers, owner-operators, REITs, property management teams, and insurance brokers to manage compliance across large portfolios of subcontractors, vendors, and tenants. Jones offers two engagement models: Jones Software (self-managed) and Jones Operator (an AI-driven concierge that runs day-to-day insurance tasks). Reported scale: 40,000+ projects, 3 billion+ square feet, and 50 million+ insurance documents processed for 300+ industry leaders. Headquartered in New York, NY, Jones was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and Foundry Group.

providers.name: Beam
providers.description: Beam is a construction financial management platform for residential and commercial contractors, headquartered in San Francisco. Its cloud software unifies estimating and proposals, progress invoicing with online payment collection, job costing and real-time profitability, expense management via the Beam Card, bill-pay automation, lien-waiver and compliance tracking, project management (daily logs, scheduling, change orders), and a cash-management account that earns cash back. Beam integrates with QuickBooks Online, CompanyCam, RenoFi and XactRemodel, and relies on vetted partners including Stripe, Footprint and CapitalOS for payments and KYC/KYB. Beam does not currently publish a public developer API, documentation surface, or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and security posture.

providers.name: Century Communities
providers.description: Century Communities is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Century Communities API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Comfort Systems USA
providers.description: Comfort Systems USA is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Comfort Systems USA API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: RPM International
providers.description: RPM International Inc. is a multinational specialty coatings and sealants company headquartered in Medina, Ohio, with annual revenues of approximately $7.4 billion. RPM operates a portfolio of over 100 leading brands across three segments: Consumer (Rust-Oleum, DAP, Zinsser), Construction (Tremco, Dryvit, Flowcrete), and Performance Coatings (Carboline, Stonhard, Plasite). RPM International does not currently offer a public developer API, but its subsidiaries and brands serve the construction, maintenance, and protective coatings markets globally.

providers.name: Sketchpro
providers.description: SketchPro is an AI copilot for Autodesk Revit that helps architects and engineers automate construction documentation directly inside their live project models. Delivered as a native Revit plugin (not a public developer API), it executes natural-language instructions to handle dimensioning, tagging, view creation, sheet setup, and scheduling, while adapting to each firm's standards, naming conventions, and documentation logic through an admin-configured AI Knowledge Base. Founded in 2023 and used by architecture practices including SOM, 10 Design, and Little, SketchPro is backed by Khosla Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or event/webhook surface; API access is described as "contact vendor / not publicly documented."

providers.name: Trunk Tools
providers.description: Trunk Tools is a construction-technology company building an AI/ML platform that helps general contractors, specialty contractors, and owners make sense of project data buried in documents and automate repetitive, time-intensive workflows. Founded in 2021 with offices in New York, Austin, and Santa Barbara, its products include TrunkText (instant answers from project documents via a construction AI agent), TrunkSubmittal and an auto-generated Submittal Register, TrunkReview (drawing-revision change detection), TrunkRFI, and TrunkBid. The platform ingests structured and unstructured construction data (PDF, XER, MPP, CSV) and connects to major project and document management systems such as Procore, Autodesk, CMiC, SharePoint, Box, Dropbox, and Egnyte. Backed by Insight Partners and Redpoint Ventures.

providers.name: Siteline
providers.description: Siteline is billing and accounts receivable software built specifically for commercial subcontractors (trade contractors). It centralizes pay applications (including AIA G702/G703 progress billing), lien waivers, lien rights, compliance documents, change orders, collections, and A/R reporting in one workflow, replacing the spreadsheets, PDFs, and GC payment-portal logins that AP/AR teams juggle every month. Siteline integrates with construction accounting systems (Sage, Foundation, Viewpoint/Vista, Spectrum, QuickBooks, Acumatica, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, CMiC, and others) and with GC payment portals (Textura, GCPay, Procore Pay) so billing data flows without double entry. Founded in 2019 by Claire Wilson and Gloria Lin, backed by Menlo Ventures and First Round Capital; subcontractors have billed over $10B across 200,000+ projects on the platform. Siteline publishes no public developer API — integrations are managed connections rather than a self-serve API.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Prenav
providers.description: PRENAV, Inc. is a Belmont, California company that automates the visual inspection of large civil and industrial structures using commercially available drones, photogrammetry and deep learning. Its PRENAV.XYZ web platform stitches thousands of drone photographs into a high-resolution 3D point-cloud digital twin, then runs machine-learning models over that twin to detect cracking in concrete, spalling, exposed rebar, cracks in steel and rust, resolving features under 0.2mm and tracking change over time. A second line, Synthetic Imagery as a Service, procedurally renders thousands of annotated photoreal defect images each month to augment a customer's own AI training sets. PRENAV publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API description; the product is sold as an enterprise service through a contact form.

providers.name: Spotlock
providers.description: Spotlock is a commodity risk management platform that helps organizations monitor, manage, and mitigate exposure to raw-material price volatility. It lets businesses track material exposures across inventory, customer contracts, and supplier commitments, set company-wide risk policies, and execute optimized hedging strategies — enabling fixed-price long-term contracts, profit margin protection, hedge accounting treatment, framework/agreement pricing, and global price intelligence for sectors such as construction and infrastructure, metal service centers and distribution, manufacturing and fabrication, automotive, energy, and transportation.

providers.name: Terra CO2
providers.description: Terra CO2 Technology is a Golden, Colorado climate-technology and building-materials manufacturer that produces low-carbon replacements for Portland cement. Its commercial product, OPUS SCM, is a supplementary cementitious material that replaces up to 50% of the Portland cement in a concrete mix as a drop-in substitute for legacy SCMs such as fly ash, cutting CO2 by roughly 70% and NOx by roughly 90% per ton replaced, and it is produced from abundant silicate feedstocks rather than coal-plant by-products. A second product, OPUS ZERO, targets a full zero-carbon cement replacement and is in concrete trials. The company runs a pilot and materials R&D facility in Golden and is building a 240,000-ton-per-year commercial plant in Cleburne, Texas, backed by more than $250M raised from climate and construction investors including Cemex Ventures. Terra CO2 sells physical material into the construction supply chain; it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Bechtel
providers.description: Bechtel is one of the largest privately held engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) companies in the world. Bechtel does not publish a public developer portal; technology integration is delivered through project-specific data exchanges with owners, joint-venture partners, and subcontractors, the Bechtel supplier portal, and industry-standard construction data exchange formats (IFC, COBie, CDE) over secure project-management platforms.

providers.name: Konn Technologies
providers.description: Konn Technologies is an Amman, Jordan based design and construction technology company, founded in 2020, that builds three integrated systems for a new model of homeownership - a composable architectural design language, an industrialized construction methodology using reinforced concrete and insulated sealed envelopes, and a software platform connecting the entire homeowner journey from first idea to keys in hand. Its consumer brand, Konn (konnhomes.com), sells that system directly to homeowners through a productized ladder - DesignFit, a 300 JOD ten-day land assessment producing 2D layouts, a site plan, and a budget and timeline; ArchDesign, a 4,000 JOD 3D design with a locked-in construction price; and Konnify, which adapts a design a homeowner already commissioned from an outside architect onto the Konn engineering system. Customer-facing software includes a Design Studio for browsing floor types, sizes, and styles with plans and pricing, and a Design Match tool that recommends a home design from stated requirements. The company reports 100+ homes designed and 35+ homes built, with typical permit-to-move-in timelines of three to six months. It publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Asap Work
providers.description: Asap.work is a next-generation temporary staffing, permanent placement, and freelance recruitment platform for the French construction and skilled-trades sector (BTP - Batiment et Travaux Publics). It connects tradespeople with short-term missions, permanent roles, and freelance projects through a mobile app and a network of consultants, and layers on worker benefits such as housing assistance, medical consultations, training via asap.academy, and wage advances. The company is backed by speedinvest and is expanding toward the United States. Asap.work publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub and, on enrichment, was confirmed to have no machine-readable API surface (searched 2026-07-18).

providers.name: Bedrock Robotics
providers.description: Bedrock Robotics develops advanced autonomy for the built world, retrofitting existing heavy construction machinery with an autonomous kit the company calls the Bedrock Operator. The system adds machine intelligence to equipment such as excavators and dozers so jobsites can run around the clock with reduced human intervention, compressing project timelines, improving safety by removing operators from hazardous work, and enabling remote progress tracking. Backed by 8vc and Emergence Capital, the company raised a $270M Series B. Bedrock is a robotics and physical-autonomy company; it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time. This profile tracks the company in the API Evangelist network and captures its public web and security posture.

providers.name: Brick&Bolt
providers.description: Brick&Bolt (bricknbolt.com) is a Bangalore-based, tech-enabled home and commercial construction marketplace that delivers end-to-end design-to-build services across major Indian cities including Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Delhi NCR, and Mysuru. The company connects homeowners with vetted contractors and manages projects through its QASCON quality system (470+ quality checks), an ESCROW-secured payment model that releases funds only as milestones complete, transparent quotations, and consumer and professional mobile apps for real-time project tracking. Backed by Accel, Brick&Bolt has delivered thousands of homes and was named to Forbes Asia's "100 to Watch" list. This profile was surfaced as an Accel portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Brick&Bolt operates a consumer construction platform and mobile apps but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: California Forever
providers.description: California Forever is a real estate and urban development company founded by Jan Sramek in 2017, backed by prominent Silicon Valley investors including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Laurene Powell Jobs, Reid Hoffman, Marc Andreessen, and Stripe co-founders Patrick and John Collison. Through its subsidiary Flannery Associates the company assembled roughly 60,000-70,000 acres of land in southeastern Solano County, California, and is planning a new walkable city for up to 400,000 residents alongside the Solano Foundry advanced manufacturing park and the Solano Shipyard. The company describes the effort as a $215 billion private investment intended to create hundreds of thousands of jobs, 170,000+ new homes, and billions in annual tax revenue over 40 years. California Forever is a physical-development and land-use company; it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable interfaces at this time.

providers.name: Iconbuild
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. (iconbuild.com) is an Austin, Texas construction technologies company using large-scale robotics, advanced materials, and software to build homes and structures. ICON develops the Vulcan and Phoenix 3D-printing robots, proprietary Lavacrete and CarbonX building materials, and design/build tooling (including its CODEX architectural catalog and ICON Prime), and has printed communities across the US as well as researched off-world construction with NASA (Project Olympus). Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a physical construction / building-technology company; as of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI, or /.well-known discovery surface, so no API artifacts were harvested.

providers.name: Improovy
providers.description: Improovy is a Chicago-based prop-tech startup and digitally-native managed marketplace that connects homeowners with vetted, professional painters and controls the end-to-end residential and commercial painting experience. Founded in 2019 by CEO Andre Kazimierski, a third-generation tradesman, the platform offers instant online quotes and covers interior and exterior house painting, cabinet painting, drywall and plaster repair, staining, power washing, and specialty finishes across markets in Illinois, Michigan, Colorado, Florida, and Wisconsin. Improovy is a consumer service brand with no public developer program or API; this profile captures its web presence and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nexii
providers.description: Nexii is a green construction technology company that designs and manufactures prefabricated wall and roof panel systems for commercial and industrial buildings. Its panels are made from Nexiite, a proprietary low-carbon building material the company says is up to 80% lighter than conventional concrete, and bolt together on site to cut build times by as much as five times while producing near-zero construction waste. Nexii serves retail, residential, warehouse, data center, cold storage, healthcare, office and education verticals, with projects for Starbucks, McDonald's, Pizza Hut, Popeyes, Dutch Bros, Walmart and Marriott. The original Vancouver-based Nexii Building Solutions entered creditor protection in January 2024; Dallas-based 3 Gates acquired its assets in a court-approved sale completed 28 June 2024 and relaunched the business as NEXII, Inc., headquartered in Dallas, Texas with manufacturing in Squamish, British Columbia. Nucor Corporation subsequently made a strategic equity investment. Nexii is a manufacturer, not a software vendor: it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Niricson Software
providers.description: Niricson Software Inc. is an infrastructure technology company making concrete infrastructure safer through AI-powered digital condition assessment. Its patented AUTOSPEX platform uses machine learning and multi-sensor data fusion (visual, thermal, and acoustic) to automatically detect, quantify, and track defects such as cracks, spalling, delamination, and alkali-aggregate reaction in dams, spillways, bridges, and airfields. Data is collected with its DRONIC architecture and NCX acoustic drone payload, which simulates the traditional concrete hammer-sounding test to identify subsurface delamination up to eight inches deep. Asset owners and civil engineers access results through the login-gated, web-based AUTOSPEX platform to interact with defect maps and compare surveys over time. Niricson operates across the USA, Canada, Australia, and India, and is a Techstars portfolio company. It exposes no public API, developer portal, or SDK at this time.

providers.name: versatile.ai
providers.description: Versatile is a construction-technology company building AI-powered crane intelligence for jobsites, primarily serving steel erectors and general contractors. Its CraneView hardware device attaches to a crane's hook block and passively captures operational data, which the Control Center software turns into real-time insight on pace, progress, productivity, and delays without asking crews to change how they work. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile Versatile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Vita Inclinata
providers.description: Vita Inclinata Technologies is a Colorado-based hardware company that builds physics-based load stabilization systems for helicopter hoists and construction cranes, eliminating the dangerous spin and sway of suspended loads. Its ecosystem spans Vita Aerospace (helicopter and rescue hoist stabilization), Vita Industrial (crane and construction load control), Air Rescue Systems (hoist training and products), and the Vita Rescue System used in military MEDEVAC operations. The company is Techstars-backed. It was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network; as a physical-hardware manufacturer it currently publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface.

providers.name: OnsiteIQ
providers.description: OnsiteIQ is a construction intelligence platform for real estate owners and developers that combines regular on-site 360-degree reality capture with AI-powered computer vision to monitor construction progress across trades and asset classes. The platform documents projects visually week over week, turns the imagery into searchable, measurable records, and surfaces analytics and actionable insights that teams use to verify progress, support payment applications, and make business-critical decisions on projects anywhere in the world. OnsiteIQ is a private company headquartered in New York City and backed by Anthemis and Bullpen Capital. As surfaced through the API Evangelist network, OnsiteIQ publishes a marketing and product website but does not expose a public developer API, documentation portal, or machine-readable API surface at this time; this profile records that honest state alongside the company's identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Togal.AI
providers.description: Togal.AI is a Miami, Florida construction-technology company building AI-powered takeoff and estimating software for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Founded by former U.S. Congressman Patrick Murphy out of his family's multi-generational construction business, the cloud-based platform applies computer-vision and deep-learning models to architectural drawings and blueprints to automatically detect, measure, count, label, and compare project spaces and features — reporting up to 98% accuracy against AIA measurement standards and reducing manual estimating effort by roughly 80%. Signature capabilities include the Togal Button (one-click automated takeoff), AI-powered image, text, and pattern search across plan sets, drawing-set comparison for change quantification, real- time multi-user cloud collaboration, and Togal.CHAT, a natural-language assistant that lets estimators query plans, verify quantities, identify errors, and draft RFPs. The product serves drywall, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, glazing, landscaping, painting, FF&E, and general-contracting trades, with documented case studies (e.g., Coastal Construction) showing multi-hour-per-plan-set savings and seven-figure annual ROI. Togal.AI's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions sold to estimators, subcontractors, and general contractors; there is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and the only known third-party integration is Service Titan plus data export to Excel and downstream estimating tools.

providers.name: Kopperfield
providers.description: Kopperfield is a software company building design and permitting tools for electrical contractors, electricians, inspectors and instructors. Founded in 2022, the company started as an EV charger installation booking service and has since become a broader contractor platform whose stated mission is to "accelerate home electrification by giving contractors the tools they need to work faster, smarter, and with total confidence." The web and mobile product covers NEC-compliant residential and commercial load calculations, drag-and-drop single line diagrams, panel schedules with circuit directories, AI panel-photo analysis, and a National Electrical Code chatbot trained on the 2017, 2020 and 2023 code editions. Kopperfield publishes a public llms.txt and a public status page but does not currently operate a public developer program: there is no published API reference, OpenAPI definition, SDK, or developer portal, and robots.txt disallows crawling of /api/. The company is backed by General Catalyst, MCJ Collective, Lachy Groom and Designer Fund.

providers.name: nPlan
providers.description: nPlan applies machine learning to construction project schedules to forecast and de-risk large capital projects. Trained on a large corpus of historical project schedules, its products (nPlan Insights Pro and nPlan Portfolio) analyze programme risk, benchmark schedules against similar projects, and surface the interventions most likely to keep delivery on time and on budget, with a Power BI integration for portfolio-level project controls. nPlan is a private enterprise SaaS company backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: ICON
providers.description: ICON Technology, Inc. is an Austin, Texas construction-technology company building large-scale robotic 3D printing systems, materials, and software to make home building faster, more affordable, and more resilient. Its flagship Titan 3D construction printer, orchestrated by the proprietary BuildOS software that translates architectural designs into robotic tool paths and manages material flow, can print the wall system of a 2,500 sq. ft. home in under seven days. ICON operates a Design + Build division delivering 3D-printed homes and communities, a Technology division selling its printers and building systems to other builders, the CODEX digital home design catalog, and ICON Prime. The company is privately held and backed by investors including Bond Capital and Pantera Capital. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a venture-portfolio lead; ICON publishes a marketing and product presence but no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Juno
providers.description: Juno (juno.co), operated by Juno Technology, Inc., is a San Francisco-based owner's representation, development-consulting and construction-management firm for prefabricated, modular and mass-timber multifamily development, working with developers from site feasibility and entitlement through delivery across North America. Juno owns the rights to the Juno Mass Timber System, a field-tested kit-of-parts building system of roughly 33 components configurable into 25+ unit types, proven on the 24-unit Juno East Austin project at 400 Comal St, Austin TX. The current company is the 2024 relaunch ("Juno 2.0") of the venture-funded Juno / Juno Residential founded in 2019 by Jonathan Scherr, BJ Siegel and Chester Chipperfield, which raised roughly $32M from Comcast Ventures, Khosla Ventures and RET Ventures before running out of money; the relaunched firm is led by co-founders Emily Mills Marineau and Jen Canchola. Juno sells professional services and a physical building system, not software: as of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing site, a mass-timber system page, a contact form, a newsletter signup, terms of service and a privacy policy, and no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Scalera
providers.description: Scalera AG is a Swiss construction-technology company building an AI platform that automates the tender and quotation process for the construction industry across the DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland). Its product-matching engine extracts positions from tender documents (PDF, GAEB, Excel/CSV, XML, email) and matches them against supplier product catalogs, while its supplier-matching tools help contractors identify relevant manufacturers and send structured inquiries. Scalera integrates with ERP, CRM, and PIM systems and serves 200+ manufacturers, processors, and traders. Backed by Speedinvest, it positions itself as one of Europe's most funded construction-tech startups. This profile documents the company's public web surface; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: TerraFirma
providers.description: TerraFirma, Inc. is a construction technology and physical-AI company building the robotic infrastructure stack for modern heavy-civil construction. Founded in 2024 by former SpaceX engineers and based in Austin, Texas, it combines AI-enabled pre-construction software (Mission Planner), a remote command-and-control center (Mission Control), and retrofitted semi-autonomous heavy machinery — excavators, bulldozers, loaders, graders and rollers operated autonomously, remotely, or traditionally. The company raised roughly $115M including a $100M Series A led by Kleiner Perkins with Bain Capital Ventures. TerraFirma publishes no public developer/API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Buildertrend
providers.description: Buildertrend is an Omaha, Nebraska-based cloud construction-management platform serving residential home builders, remodelers, and specialty trade contractors. The product consolidates sales (CRM, leads, proposals, contracts, email marketing), project management (schedule, daily logs, selections, change orders, warranties, sub portal, client updates), and financial management (estimates, bids, takeoff, job-costing budgets, bills, purchase orders, invoices, online payments) into a single web and mobile application used by 20,000+ builders. Pricing is custom-quoted by sales rather than published self-serve tiers, with unlimited users and projects on every plan, and the platform integrates with QuickBooks, Xero, and other accounting and trade tools through a partner integrations marketplace. The company exposes a REST API at api.buildertrend.com that is gated by partner agreement — endpoints return 401 Unauthorized to the public and there is no open developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API key signup. As a result Buildertrend is profiled here as a non-public (partner-only) API provider; the public surface documented is limited to marketing, support, integrations marketplace, mobile apps, and corporate resources.

providers.name: Carlisle Companies
providers.description: Carlisle Companies Incorporated (NYSE: CSL) is a global diversified manufacturer of highly engineered building envelope products and solutions, serving commercial and residential construction, insulation, roofing, waterproofing, and specialty markets. Carlisle's primary operating segment is Carlisle Construction Materials (CCM), which includes brands such as Carlisle SynTec Systems, Hunter Panels, Henry Company, MB Technology, and WIP Industrial. Carlisle does not publish a public developer API; distributors and direct contractors transact through the Carlisle Customer Success Portal, and commercial trading partners integrate with Carlisle using standard X12 EDI transactions (850, 855, 856, 810) over AS2/SFTP.

providers.name: OpenSpace
providers.description: OpenSpace is a visual intelligence platform for the construction industry, headquartered at 333 Kearny Street, San Francisco, California. The company pairs an off-the-shelf 360-degree camera worn on a hardhat with computer-vision software that automatically maps captured imagery to construction floor plans and BIM models, producing a navigable, time-indexed visual record of every jobsite walk. The platform is built around five products: Capture (complete visual record), Field (image-based task management with AI Autolocation), Track (AI-driven progress tracking against schedule), Air (drone imagery management), and BIM+ (3D field tools). OpenSpace reports more than 69 billion square feet captured across projects in 131 countries, with regional presence in Australia, Canada, EU, Japan, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, and the United Kingdom. The company is led by CEO and co-founder Jeevan Kalanithi. OpenSpace integrates with the major construction software stacks, including Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud / Autodesk Build, Revizto, PlanGrid, and Bluebeam. A REST API exists for partner and enterprise integration but is not publicly self-serve; integration access is obtained via OpenSpace's support and partner channels.

providers.name: Emidat
providers.description: Emidat GmbH is a Munich-based climate technology company building product intelligence infrastructure for the construction industry. Its SaaS platform lets construction material manufacturers create verified Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), run Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs), and produce Digital Product Passports (DPPs) at scale. Emidat ingests plant, ERP, and energy-management data through integrations, performs intelligent data matching, and generates ISO-compliant, verified EPDs in as little as a day rather than the typical six to twelve months. The platform also surfaces environmental-impact hotspots so manufacturers can find emission-reduction opportunities and turn sustainability data into business value. Related tools include the public EPD Database and Emidat Atlas.

providers.name: Parsons Corporation
providers.description: Parsons Corporation is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Parsons Corporation API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Reiner.ai
providers.description: Reiner.ai (operated by AI Mapping GmbH of Cologne, Germany) is a construction- and planning-industry AI platform for architects, engineers, and planners. It combines leading LLMs with domain-specific "Reiner Knowledge" and "Reiner Logic" layers to deliver Reiner Chat, task-specific KI-Agenten (AI agents) for site protocols, explanatory reports and project applications, company-knowledge integration, and a library of 50+ prebuilt construction prompts. The product is delivered as a hosted web application (app.reiner.ai); as of this enrichment pass there is no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Jumba
providers.description: Jumba is a Nairobi-based construction technology company founded in 2022 that digitizes the sourcing and financing of construction materials across Africa. Its B2B marketplace connects hardware retail stores and construction sites to manufacturers and suppliers of materials such as cement, steel, tiles, plumbing, electrical, paint and finishes, offering real-time price comparison and online ordering. Jumba OS is a management application for tracking sales, inventory and creditor accounts, while Jengwa provides buy-now-pay-later inventory financing. The company operates a consumer mobile app and reports processing over 12.6 million cement bags through more than 1,350 hardware stores, and is backed by Speedinvest. Jumba does not publish a public API; its developer presence is limited to open-source tooling on its GitHub organization.

providers.name: TEDI
providers.description: TEDI (Tecnologia y Educacion Innovadora) is a Latin American EdTech platform delivering professional training for the construction and engineering industries under the motto "Mejores profesionales, mejores paises." It runs 150+ live and recorded courses each month covering BIM, VDC, Lean management, and project management, plus Autodesk/PMI-aligned certifications, an exclusive construction job board, a professional community, the EDI AI learning assistant, and a TEDICOINS rewards system. TEDI reports 50,000+ certified students across 18+ countries with 150+ expert instructors, and is backed by 500 Global. The company operates a consumer-facing web platform (tedivirtual.com / tedicomunidad.com) and, as of this enrichment pass, publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Higharc
providers.description: Higharc is an AI-powered homebuilding software platform founded in 2018 by Marc Minor and headquartered in Durham, North Carolina, with team members across San Francisco and Atlanta. Its design-to-construction cloud platform lets residential builders design homes from scratch, configure market-proven plans, and turn every home into shoppable 3D visuals, plan-based estimating data, and permit-ready construction documents. The product surface spans Studio (design), Config (plan configuration), Showroom (3D visualization), Estimate (material takeoffs), Build (construction documents), Photoreal (renderings), and enterprise AI Estimating, unifying architecture, sales, and construction operations. Higharc is a portfolio company of Fifth Wall and was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profiling it publishes no public developer API, reference, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Aeroseal
providers.description: Aeroseal is a building-envelope and duct air-sealing technology company headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio. Its patented aerosol sealing process — developed by Dr. Mark Modera under U.S. Department of Energy research at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory beginning in 1993 and commercialized as Aeroseal in 2010 — injects a fog of non-toxic sealant particles into a pressurized duct system or building envelope, where the particles collect at the edges of leaks and seal them from the inside. The company sells computer-controlled sealing equipment and software to a dealer network under the HomeSeal Connect and AeroBarrier Connect product lines; the on-machine software measures leakage in real time and issues a certificate of completion showing before-and-after leakage rates. Aeroseal reports operations in 27 countries and all 50 U.S. states, and has raised roughly $119M across three rounds, including a $67M Series B in July 2023 backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Climate Investment and OGCI. It is an equipment, materials and contractor-software business rather than a developer platform: it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Arcol
providers.description: Arcol is a browser-based, real-time collaborative building design and documentation platform for the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry, often described as a "Figma for BIM." Founded in 2021 by Paul O'Carroll and based in New York City, Arcol keeps massing, floorplans, metrics, estimating, and construction documentation connected in a single cloud-native workspace so early design decisions stay constructible. It supports multiplayer editing (built on Liveblocks), IFC and Excel import/export, a Rhino integration, and AI-assisted modeling. Arcol is backed by Cowboy Ventures and Craft Ventures. A public plugin API and developer SDK are described on the roadmap but are not yet published, so this profile currently exposes no programmatic API surface.

providers.name: Trayd
providers.description: Trayd is a construction payroll, HR, and compliance platform built for commercial trade contractors and subcontractors. It automates certified and prevailing-wage payroll, union and multi-state compliance reporting, field and labor tracking, crew scheduling and dispatch, HR onboarding and benefits, and offers same-day pay, moving tens of millions of payroll dollars each week. Founded in 2022 (Y Combinator S23) and backed by Bloomberg Beta, Trayd operates a private SaaS and mobile application with no public developer API, documentation, or integration surface published at this time.

providers.name: Universal Forest Products
providers.description: UFP Industries (formerly Universal Forest Products) is a leading global manufacturer and distributor of wood and wood-alternative products serving retail, industrial, and construction markets. UFP operates over 200 facilities globally supplying lumber, engineered wood products, packaging, and building materials. The company has integrated OnBase-based business system integration for document management and workflow automation across its supply chain operations.

providers.name: Vulcan Materials Company
providers.description: Vulcan Materials Company is the nation's largest producer of construction aggregates, primarily crushed stone, sand, and gravel, and a major producer of asphalt mix and ready-mixed concrete. Headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama, Vulcan serves all 50 states and operates over 400 quarries and plants. As a Fortune 500 company, Vulcan serves the construction industry with materials critical for roads, bridges, buildings, and infrastructure. Vulcan does not publish a public developer API ecosystem; their digital operations focus on internal ERP systems, supplier portals, and customer order management platforms.

providers.name: Blox
providers.description: BLOX is a Bessemer, Alabama design-manufacture-construct (DMC) company that describes itself as the largest manufacturer of healthcare buildings in the United States. Founded in 2010-2011 as a spinoff of Giattina Aycock Architecture Studio by Chris Giattina, BLOX designs, prefabricates and installs modular medical buildings and building components — freestanding emergency departments, acute-care patient-room modules, primary-care clinics and full hospitals — from a former Pullman Standard railcar plant in the Interstate Industrial Park. Customers include HCA Healthcare, Encompass Health, Universal Health Services and Walmart Health. The company is privately held and its shares appear on secondary-market venues such as Forge Global. BLOX publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable specification; its software work is internal tooling for the DMC delivery system rather than a product.

providers.name: Cornerstone Building Brands
providers.description: Cornerstone Building Brands is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Cornerstone Building Brands API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: iControl
providers.description: iControl is a Swedish construction-technology company whose mobile application digitalizes documentation on construction sites, replacing paper-based protocols and inspection records with real-time digital capture. Field personnel create, share, and manage project documentation from the job site, with offline capture that syncs when connectivity returns, drawing and blueprint uploads, and team collaboration. Marketed under the promise "Skriv aldrig ett protokoll igen" (never write a protocol again), iControl is used by leading Nordic contractors including NCC, JM, Veidekke, ARCONA, and In3prenor across infrastructure, residential, commercial, and public-facility projects. The company is headquartered in Stockholm and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. iControl exposes a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Pillar Technologies
providers.description: Pillar Technologies provides construction jobsite risk management through environmental monitoring and data analytics. Its wireless, rugged "Pod" sensors measure eight environmental metrics on the jobsite (temperature, humidity, carbon monoxide, VOCs, particulates, noise, light, and pressure) with cellular connectivity and a one-year battery life, feeding a real-time software platform with customizable dashboards, floorplan integration, and drill-down reporting by site, floor, or sensor. A configurable alert system notifies teams via text, email, or phone. Pillar serves data centers, hospitality and multi-family housing, and science and healthcare construction projects to improve safety and protect schedules and budgets. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: TigerEye
providers.description: TigerEye is an AI company for the construction industry, helping builders get answers faster and spend less time searching for information across construction, business intelligence, and home planning and delivery workflows. Founded as an Initialized Capital-backed startup and acquired by homebuilder Lennar to scale its capabilities nationally, TigerEye operates a public marketing site with an About page, Terms of Use, and Privacy Policy. As of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, documentation, or well-known discovery surface, and its former Secureframe-hosted trust center now redirects to a 404.

providers.name: Autositu
providers.description: Autositu (AutoSitu) is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) PropTech startup building an AI-native intelligence layer for real estate development plan review. Its multi-agent platform automatically analyzes site plans, building plans, and AEC drawings against municipal zoning and building codes to flag compliance issues before submission, cutting city comments and resubmittals so approvals move faster. The product serves cities, architecture and engineering firms, and real estate developers with human-in-the-loop review workflows. Autositu is an early-stage SaaS company and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as an enrichment lead.

providers.name: Officebanao
providers.description: Officebanao is a technology-enabled office interior design and build company headquartered in Gurugram and Bengaluru, India, and founded in 2021. It delivers turnkey commercial workspace solutions — space planning, interior design, furniture procurement, office renovation, and end-to-end project execution — for startups, enterprises, and coworking spaces across 40+ Indian cities. Its "Tech plus Touch" delivery model pairs real-time 3D visualization and online progress tracking with an in-house team of designers and project managers. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners. Officebanao publishes a public marketing website and an llms.txt discovery file but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer platform surface as of this profiling.

providers.name: Buildcheck
providers.description: Buildcheck is a Sweden-based cloud software platform that simplifies self-inspections and quality checklists for construction and infrastructure projects. The service uses AI to automatically generate project-specific inspection and control plans from uploaded building documents, then lets field teams document work on a mobile app with photo capture and digital signatures, share progress with clients through shareable links, and export organized PDF reports. It offers company-branded templates, role-based access, SSO and other enterprise features. Buildcheck was founded by Anders Jacobson (previously Next One Technology) and Johnny Wulcan (founder of Byggplanen). It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API or API documentation has been found on its site as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Bobyard
providers.description: Bobyard is an AI takeoff and estimating software company for the construction industry. Its platform reads construction drawings and blueprints to automatically extract quantities and organize takeoffs, cutting manual estimation work by 50-90% for trade contractors in landscaping, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and finishes.
