Trained on millions of drawings, Bobyard automates AI takeoff, manual takeoff, OC conversions, and estimate generation so contractors can increase bid capacity without expanding estimating staff. Bobyard was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes product documentation and a live status page (including an Inference API component) but does not currently expose a public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDKs.

providers.name: Augmenta
providers.description: Augmenta is a Toronto-based generative AI company building the Augmenta Construction Platform (ACP), a Spatial AI system that automates building design — starting with electrical raceway routing and expanding into mechanical and plumbing (MEP). ACP ingests Revit models, accepts conduit run schedules, fly/no-fly zones, and project specifications, then generates clash-free, constructable 3D conduit routes in the cloud and exports them back into Revit as system conduit ready for detailing and prefabrication. The platform combines computational geometry, advanced optimization, and machine learning to handle data-center, hospital, and school-scale electrical builds, and is marketed to VDC teams and electrical contractors as a way to cut BIM time by roughly two-thirds. Augmenta was founded by veterans of generative design for advanced manufacturing, won EC&M 2026 Product of the Year, was named to the 2026 Global Cleantech 100, and signed a five-year strategic partnership with E-J Electric Installation Co. The product is delivered as a SOC2-certified Revit add-in with a cloud back-end; there is no public REST API, SDK, or open-source release.

providers.name: Crewline
providers.description: Crewline is an autonomous heavy-equipment company that retrofits existing construction machinery to operate self-driving. Its hardware retrofit kit installs on-site in about an hour and adds autonomy to drum rollers today (compatible with Caterpillar, Bomag, Hamm, Volvo, and CASE), with dozers on the 2027 roadmap and rock trucks, excavators, motor graders, and wheel loaders in development. It is offered on a subscription model with zero upfront cost, a fixed monthly rate per machine, and 24/7 technical support, targeting earthworks and grading crews. Crewline is backed by Initialized Capital and headquartered in San Francisco. It publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Freemodel
providers.description: Freemodel is a presale home renovation platform that helps real estate agents and homeowners prepare properties for sale by coordinating design, renovation, and project management through local project directors. It offers pay-at-close financing so clients can defer renovation costs until the home sells, and provides transparent online project tracking. Freemodel operates across Northern California (Bay Area, Sonoma, Santa Cruz/Monterey) and Southwest Florida. This profile was surfaced as a QED Investors portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Freemodel publishes no public API or developer program at this time.

providers.name: Knowify
providers.description: Knowify is a New York-based construction management SaaS for trade contractors (electrical, plumbing, HVAC, painting, remodeling, concrete, excavation), covering the full job lifecycle from bidding through payment on a single platform. The product spans project execution (estimating, proposals and contracts, change orders, RFIs and submittals, scheduling, daily logs, document and photo management), service work (dispatch, invoicing, payments, field operations, asset and inventory management), and financial management (AIA billing, job costing, prevailing wage, purchase orders, expenses, WIP and reporting). Knowify is positioned as the official construction software partner of QuickBooks Online and offers deep two-way sync with QuickBooks Online, QuickBooks Desktop, Intuit Enterprise Suite, QuickBooks Payroll, QuickBooks Payments, and QuickBooks Time, alongside native integrations with CompanyCam, Billd, Lumber, eBacon, and AIA Contract Documents. Third-party automation is available via Zapier. Pricing starts at $99/month (Core), $249/month (Advanced), and custom Enterprise, with paid add-ons for Service Pro, Live Equipment Tracking (FleetSharp), AI Dashcams, and Tool Tracking. Knowify does not publish a public REST API, webhooks specification, SDK, CLI, or developer portal; programmatic access for third parties is limited to Zapier and the QuickBooks ecosystem.

providers.name: Material Evolution
providers.description: Material Evolution is a UK-based cleantech manufacturer of ultra-low carbon cement for the construction industry. Its MevoCem and MevoXL products use a proprietary "Alkali Fusion" process to transform industrial byproducts into cement feedstocks, achieving a 52.5N strength rating at roughly 144-196 kg CO2e per tonne versus ordinary Portland cement. The company operates compact, automated factories (including its Wrexham facility) and applies AI to material development and feedstock optimization. It is a B2B cement supplier and does not currently publish any public developer-facing API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Reno
providers.description: Reno (Reno Home) is a Dubai, UAE based one-stop home renovation platform that connects homeowners and businesses with professional interior designers and vetted contractors, managing renovation projects end-to-end from design and contracting through quality inspections and completion. Its Reno mobile app lets clients track project progress, budgets, timelines and change requests in real time, and it offers a "Renovate Now, Pay Later" financing model with 3, 6 or 12 month installment plans. Reno is backed by 500 Global (500 Sanabil), Hub71 and other regional investors. It is a consumer-facing service and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Torus
providers.description: Torus is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building an AI-powered engineering intelligence platform for capital projects. Its agents analyze engineering documents such as P&IDs, datasheets, specification sheets, and drawings to extract parameters, flag cross-document inconsistencies across 50+ categories, and automate workflow deliverables like procurement approvals and RFIs for infrastructure, data center, and energy projects. Torus runs as a managed cloud or a sovereign in-VPC deployment and publishes no public API or developer surface as of July 2026.

providers.name: ALICE Technologies
providers.description: ALICE Technologies is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company that builds an AI-driven generative scheduling and construction optioneering platform. The product simulates millions of possible construction sequences for a project — varying crews, equipment, methods, and constraints — to find optimal schedules, accelerate timelines, recover delayed projects, and de-risk capital project delivery. ALICE's suite includes ALICE Optimize (generative scheduling from imported Primavera P6 or Microsoft Project schedules), ALICE Plan (a 2D visual planning canvas overlaid on drawings), ALICE Model (BIM-driven schedule generation from 3D models), and the Schedule Insights Agent (an LLM-powered conversational interface for analysing and recommending schedule changes, including automated DCMA 14-point schedule quality scoring). The platform is sold as SaaS to general contractors, owners and developers, and consultants working on industrial (data centres, energy, semiconductors), infrastructure (rail, highway, tunnels), and commercial projects, with reported impacts including up to 17% reduction in project duration and 14% labor cost savings. ALICE was founded in 2015 by René Morkos (Stanford PhD) and is backed by Merus Capital, Foundamental, Future Ventures, Lightspeed, Blackhorn Ventures, and Brick and Mortar; in 2026 it announced a formal alliance with McKinsey to deploy generative scheduling on capital projects. ALICE integrates by importing from Primavera P6, Primavera Cloud, Microsoft Project, and BIM/drawing formats, but does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source repository — integration is delivered via the product's import/export surface and customer-success engagements.

providers.name: Craftview
providers.description: Craftview Software GmbH is a Frankfurt-headquartered European software group that builds ERP and project-management software for the skilled trades. Formed as a buy-and-build platform, Craftview operates a portfolio of long-established regional ERP brands — C'FLUIDE, ES2000, EXTRABAT, GILDE, KS21, MOSER, OSD, PLENION, RITA BOSSE and WINWORKER — serving green industries, construction-related trades, technical services and specialized crafts across Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands and France. The group reports 25,000+ active customers, 330+ employees and 11 locations across 41 key European regions. Craftview publishes no public developer portal, API documentation or machine-readable API definitions; its software is sold and delivered per brand as on-premise and cloud ERP for trade businesses.

providers.name: Assembly OSM
providers.description: Assembly OSM is a New York City off-site manufacturing company founded in 2019 by SHoP Architects co-founders Bill and Chris Sharples to industrialise the construction of high-rise urban housing. The company calls its method "post-modular": rather than trucking finished volumetric boxes from a single factory, Assembly designs a kit-of-parts chassis and distributes fabrication across a network of specialist suppliers — an aerospace and automotive supply-chain model applied to buildings — then stacks the resulting units on site, claiming delivery of market-competitive high-rise residential architecture in roughly 60% of conventional schedule. Its buildings are all-electric and passive-design led, targeting 55-70% energy-efficiency improvement and 35% less embodied carbon today, net-zero operational carbon by 2027 and climate-positive buildings by 2040. Completed and in-progress work includes Prototype Alpha, 147 St. Felix Street and 247 East 117th Street in New York, plus an AOSM Canada operation. The company has raised more than $60 million, including a $38 million Series A in 2022, and draws engineering staff from SpaceX, Tesla and Boeing. Assembly runs a digital-twin engineering platform — a heavily scripted CATIA environment carrying each module from design through fabrication to installation — but that platform is an internal manufacturing tool, not a product: Assembly OSM sells buildings, and publishes no developer program, no public API, no SDK and no machine-readable API contract of any kind.

providers.name: Dycom Industries
providers.description: Dycom Industries is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Dycom Industries API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Buildots
providers.description: Buildots is an AI-powered construction intelligence platform headquartered in Tel Aviv, Israel, with offices in London and the United States. The company combines 360-degree hardhat-mounted cameras with computer vision and machine learning models that automatically capture, locate, and classify on-site construction progress against the project BIM model and schedule, producing trade-level performance data, deviation and delay detection, and portfolio-wide analytics for general contractors, project teams, executives, and owners. Buildots reports that projects using the platform together with a performance-driven operating approach have reduced delays by up to 50%. The product family includes Buildots (the AI construction intelligence platform), Genda (workforce intelligence), and a fully managed Capture Services operation that handles routine site capture for customers. Verticals served include data centers, commercial, multifamily, healthcare, industrial, education, and airports. Notable customers shown on the website include Intel, Mortenson, JE Dunn, Turner, Wates, and STO. Buildots was founded in 2018 and is led by CEO and co-founder Roy Danon with co-founders Aviv Leibovici (CPO) and Yakir Sudry (CCO). Investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Future Energy Ventures, Viola Ventures, TLV Partners, OG Ventures, and Tencent. Buildots does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integrations with construction software (e.g., Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud) are arranged directly through the company.

providers.name: Urban Machine
providers.description: Urban Machine is a GV-backed robotics company building AI and computer-vision powered machines that remove metal fasteners (nails, staples, and screws) from construction and demolition lumber waste, reclaiming it for premium wood products and circular-economy reuse. The company publishes no public API, but maintains an open-source ROS/Python robotics tooling footprint on GitHub, including the colcon-poetry-ros package on PyPI.

providers.name: Mighty Buildings
providers.description: Mighty Buildings is a construction-technology and advanced-manufacturing company that industrializes homebuilding using large-format 3D printing, proprietary polymer-composite materials and robotic automation. Founded in 2019 and originally based in Oakland, California, it raised more than $150 million from investors including Khosla Ventures, Bold Capital and Aramco's Wa'ed Ventures, and was the first company certified under the UL 3401 standard for evaluating building structures and assemblies, as well as being certified under California's Factory Built Housing program. Its current product is the Mighty Kit System / Mighty Wall System - factory-made complete wall panels that arrive on site with integrated structure, insulation, waterproofing and exterior finish, so builders assemble a building envelope with conventional methods and fewer on-site steps. After a January 2025 restructuring and sale process, the full suite of Mighty Buildings technologies was acquired by LUMUS Inc., and Mighty Buildings now operates as a LUMUS brand headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon. The company sells physical building systems to developers and builders; it operates no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Sadbhav Engineering Limited
providers.description: Sadbhav Engineering Limited (SEL), operating at sadbhaveng.com, is an Indian infrastructure and civil-engineering contractor founded in 1988 by Vishnubhai M. Patel and headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The company builds and operates large-scale roads and highways, mining, and irrigation projects, including Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) concessions of national significance, and is publicly listed on the NSE and BSE. This is a traditional infrastructure/construction firm: it publishes an investor-relations and corporate website but exposes no developer API, SDK, documentation, or other machine-readable API surface. Surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a stub via vc-portfolio harvesting; an enrichment pass confirmed there is no API product to catalog.

providers.name: Sensmore
providers.description: Sensmore (sensmore GmbH) is a German industrial-automation and embodied-AI company that turns robotics research into field-proven systems for heavy machinery in raw material operations. Its platform connects machines, sites, and data across mining, aggregates/construction, and defense, spanning products including Site Intelligence (live site operations), Machine Assist (driver assistance and collision warning), Eye (visual monitoring), Live Mapping (real-time site mapping), and Loader Automation (autonomous vehicle systems), with claims of reducing downtime by up to 30% while improving safety and resource efficiency. Sensmore was surfaced as a portfolio company of Point Nine and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or developer documentation; its web presence is a marketing and corporate site.

providers.name: SupplyHog
providers.description: SupplyHog is an ecommerce platform built specifically for hardware and building-materials retailers, giving independent hardware and building-supply stores a branded online storefront to sell their products. The platform provides co-op and custom product catalogs, flexible fulfillment (in-store pickup, ship-to-store, local delivery, and ship-to-home with Shippo shipping labels), Stripe-powered payments, TaxJar tax calculation, real-time ERP inventory and pricing synchronization, custom branding and domains, location-aware search, and admin tools for order fulfillment and abandoned-cart recovery. Founded in 2010 as the Nopone.com reverse-auction marketplace, SupplyHog went through the DreamIt and 500 Startups accelerators, pivoted to full ecommerce services, and was acquired by construction-supply retailer R.P. Lumber in 2016. It does not publish a public developer API surface; it acts as a consumer of Stripe, TaxJar, and Shippo.

providers.name: Armstrong World Industries
providers.description: Armstrong World Industries (NYSE: AWI) is a leading global designer and manufacturer of innovative commercial and residential ceiling, wall, and suspension system solutions. Armstrong offers a broad portfolio of ceiling and wall products across mineral fiber, fiberglass, wood, metal, and specialty substrates for use in commercial construction and renovation projects worldwide. The company provides BIM content, product data, and specification tools for architects and designers but does not offer a public developer API.

providers.name: Peter Kiewit Sons'
providers.description: Peter Kiewit Sons' (Kiewit Corporation) is one of North America's largest and most respected construction and engineering organizations, working on projects in transportation, water, oil, gas, power, and building markets. This repository tracks any publicly available APIs, SDKs, and developer resources for Kiewit.

providers.name: Xiaopangxiong
providers.description: Xiaopangxiong (小胖熊, "small fat bear") is a Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for home and office renovation materials, operated by Shanghai Miju Network Technology Co., Ltd. (上海米居网络科技有限公司). The platform connects building-material suppliers with renovation contractors, crew foremen, and decoration companies, selling the full range of auxiliary materials (辅材) — sand, cement, paint and coatings, electrical wiring, pipes, tiles, and leveling supplies — through a self-operated model that spans factory-direct procurement, warehousing, logistics, delivery, installation, and after-sales service. Headquartered in Shanghai with service stations and warehouses in Suzhou, Hangzhou, Hefei, Ningbo, Wuxi, and Jiaxing, Xiaopangxiong is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and distributes primarily through its 小胖熊 mobile app; the company publishes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD
providers.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

providers.name: Monumental
providers.description: Monumental builds autonomous construction robots and the software that runs them. Its robots lay bricks and blockwork on real building sites, coordinated by Monumental's software platform (Atrium) and fleet operations (Fleet). The venture-backed company operates across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, and the United States, and has raised multiple funding rounds (including a reported $32M raise and Series B rounds in the US and UK). Monumental was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation - this record captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Bitacora.io
providers.description: Bitacora.io is a Mexican field-data and operations platform (a 500 Global / 500 LatAm Batch 14 startup) that helps deskless teams in construction, maintenance, and field services capture reports, photos, tasks, and events from the field. Its mobile and web apps work offline and sync to the cloud when connectivity returns, turning field activity into searchable records, PDF and Excel exports, map and gallery views, and real-time analytics dashboards for managers. Bitacora is a SaaS product rather than a developer-API company - it offers custom development, integrations, and KPI dashboards as professional services, but does not publish a public self-serve API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK.

providers.name: Beazer Homes USA
providers.description: Beazer Homes USA, Inc. (NYSE: BZH) is an Atlanta, Georgia-headquartered national homebuilder founded in 1985 and publicly listed since 1994. The company designs, sells, and builds single-family and multi-family homes across approximately thirteen U.S. states under brand differentiators such as Choice Plans (customizable floorplans), Mortgage Choice (competitive lender program), Style Choice (interior personalization), and Livable Features (accessibility options). Beazer markets itself as "America's #1 Energy-Efficient Homebuilder," citing homes that are 44% more efficient than the average HERS-rated new home and shipping whole-house ERV ventilation in 100% of homes. As of the most recent public data point (FY2016 10-K), Beazer reported revenue of $1.822B, delivered 5,419 homes, operated 161 active communities, and employed approximately 1,100 people. The company has no public developer program or external APIs; its digital surface is a consumer-facing marketing/community-finder website plus an investor relations portal.

providers.name: Knife River
providers.description: Knife River Corporation is one of the leading aggregates-led construction materials and contracting companies in the United States. The company mines, processes, and sells construction aggregates, ready-mix concrete, asphalt, and related products, and also performs heavy-civil construction services. Knife River operates across multiple western and central U.S. states.

providers.name: Saint-Gobain
providers.description: Saint-Gobain is a French multinational corporation founded in 1665, headquartered in Courbevoie, France. It designs, manufactures, and distributes materials and solutions for the construction, mobility, healthcare, and industrial markets. The group operates through well-known brands including CertainTeed (North American roofing, insulation, gypsum), Norton (abrasives), Weber (mortars and facades), Placo (plasterboard, France), and ISOVER (insulation). Saint-Gobain trades on Euronext Paris under the ticker SGO and is a component of the CAC 40 and Euro Stoxx 50 indices. As a building materials and industrial manufacturer, Saint-Gobain operates no public developer program, API portal, or machine-readable surface. The GitHub organization at github.com/saint-gobain exists but hosts zero public repositories. Any digital integration with customers, distributors, or partners happens through private B2B channels (EDI, custom integrations, e-commerce portals for trade buyers) rather than a documented public API. This repo exists in the API Evangelist network as a placeholder record for the company — to mark that the surface area was assessed and found to be absent — rather than to catalog APIs.

providers.name: Skycatch
providers.description: Skycatch built spatial data capture, processing, and analytics for mining and construction sites, turning drone and aerial imagery into high-precision 3D data, volumetrics, and AI-driven site insights. Its products included Spatial Sight, Spatial DataHub (datahub.skycatch.com), and EdgeServer for on-site edge processing. Skycatch was acquired by Caterpillar Inc. on July 7, 2026 (following Caterpillar's RPMGlobal acquisition) to expand its mining technology capabilities. A developer platform exists at docs.skycatch.com but is password-gated, and no public API specification is available. Originally surfaced as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company.

providers.name: Tradeway
providers.description: Tradeway is an AI-powered field assistant for residential trade contractors working in electrical, plumbing, and HVAC. Technicians use it to plan jobs step by step with the right materials and code requirements, to identify parts from a photo with nearby supplier pricing and sourcing, and to get hands-free answers to technical questions on the job site. For business owners it centralizes crew history and field activity into a single view, reducing callbacks and rework through built-in code checks and standardized, repeatable processes so new hires can bill like veterans. Tradeway is backed by Bloomberg Beta. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Brik
providers.description: Brik ("[Re]Constructing Construction") is an Indonesian construction-materials company, backed by Accel, that operates concrete batching plants and supplies ready-mix concrete for building and infrastructure projects across the Greater Jakarta region, including Bekasi, Bogor, Karawang, and Bandung. Its product line spans standard ready-mix batches and higher-performance "Super Concrete" variants used for mass-concrete pours. At the time of enrichment Brik publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook surface; this record is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Buildcon
providers.description: Buildcon is a Belgrade-based construction and logistics digitalisation company that builds Buildx, a proprietary construction project management platform covering project scheduling, cost tracking, daily logs, installed-quantities tracking, and reporting, alongside Buildx Warehouse for warehouse management and Buildx Tracking for real-time asset tracking. The team pairs deep construction and logistics domain knowledge with a modern web stack (React, Angular, Node.js, PostgreSQL on AWS/DigitalOcean) to help builders and logistics operators move off spreadsheets and onto connected operational software. Buildcon is a portfolio company backed by 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface.

providers.name: ConXtech
providers.description: ConXtech is a Pleasanton, California structural steel subcontractor that designs, fabricates, delivers and erects prefabricated steel building frames for commercial construction. Its ConX Systems product line — the XL-400 and XR-200 chassis — uses patented collar-and-column connection technology and AISC 358 seismic prequalification to erect frames the company reports are three to five times faster than traditional steel erection, across healthcare, data center, retail, office, education, high-density residential, hospitality, industrial and government projects totalling more than 20 million square feet. ConXtech is a private company; its equity trades on secondary markets. It sells a physical building system, not software, and publishes no public developer program, API or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Levelset
providers.description: Levelset is a New Orleans-based construction payment software company that helps contractors, subcontractors, material suppliers, and equipment rental firms manage mechanics lien rights, preliminary notices, lien waivers, and payment compliance across all 50 U.S. states. The platform automates preliminary notice delivery, lien filing and release, conditional and unconditional lien waiver exchange, job and stakeholder research, and contractor payment-history monitoring, with deep state-by-state lien-law templates and deadline tracking. Founded as zlien in 2011 and rebranded to Levelset in 2018, the company was acquired by Procore Technologies for approximately $500 million in November 2021 and now operates as part of Procore's invoicing and payments suite. Customer-facing integrations exist with Procore, Sage, Viewpoint, Foundation, Acumatica, QuickBooks and other construction ERP and accounting platforms, but Levelset does not currently publish a self-serve public REST API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal — integrations are delivered through partner-built connectors, the Procore Marketplace, and direct enterprise engagements with the Levelset integrations team. The Levelset GitHub organization is empty and developers.levelset.com / developer.levelset.com are not publicly reachable as of this profile date.

providers.name: Daero Group
providers.description: DAERO (Daero Group) is a construction-technology company building mobile-first tools for trades and field teams. Its flagship product, ZeroPunch, is a field-operations platform that turns real-time field intuition into structured construction data: voice-first capture lets crews speak field observations in natural language, photos are paired with contextual field data, work is auto-assigned by scope, and stream-of-consciousness notes are converted into organized daily logs. ZeroPunch offers a two-way integration with Procore for project-management sync. The company positions itself around the daily needs of the people actually doing the work, aiming to make construction operations smarter and faster. As of this profile DAERO publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; integration is partnership-level (Procore) and inquiries go to support@daerogroup.com. Backed by Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Fixed
providers.description: Fixed (fixed.com.au) is a Brisbane, Australia based construction, refurbishment and facility-maintenance company specialising in the childcare sector. The business delivers centre refurbishments, reactive and preventative maintenance, emergency repairs, landscaping and outdoor play-space (yard) services for childcare and early-learning facilities across Australia, with licensed and inducted teams and 24/7 after-hours availability. It is a services trades business with a WordPress marketing website and no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable surface. This entry was auto-created as a stub from a venture-portfolio match; that match is almost certainly a domain/name collision (see x-notes) and the profile is retained here as an enriched, no-API-surface company record.

providers.name: EMCOR Group
providers.description: EMCOR Group is a Fortune 500 mechanical and electrical construction, energy, and facilities services company headquartered in Norwalk, Connecticut. It operates through three segments, EMCOR Construction Services, EMCOR Building Services, and EMCOR Industrial Services, delivering hyperscale data center construction, hospital support services, energy efficiency programs, and green building solutions. This repository captures the public APIs, developer resources, and machine-readable artifacts associated with EMCOR Group.

providers.name: Muro AI
providers.description: Muro AI is an early-stage construction-technology startup building PrecOS, a pre-construction operating system marketed as a pre-con manager's AI assistant that carries general contractors from scoping through handover. The platform applies domain-adapted large language models, image models, agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, and document/plan parsing (OCR and computer vision) to automate bid comparison, estimation, bill-of-materials, and budget updates for teams that still run on spreadsheets. Muro is backed by Techstars and integrates with industry tools such as Procore. As of this profiling the company publishes a marketing site, a blog, and careers pages, but exposes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation, so this record captures identity and a domain-security probe rather than an API surface.

providers.name: United Dwelling
providers.description: United Dwelling was a Los Angeles-based real estate development company founded in 2018 by venture capitalist Steven Dietz to address the affordable housing shortage by converting underused garages and backyards into accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The company offered studio, one-bedroom, and two-bedroom zero-net-carbon units ranging from 328 to 647 square feet and handled permitting, construction, financing, and property management end to end. It raised a $10 million Series B in May 2020 led by Alpha Edison with participation from Lightspeed Venture Partners. The business appears to have wound down - its website has lapsed (Squarespace account expired) and its Los Angeles location is marked closed as of mid-2026 - and it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: USG
providers.description: USG Corporation is a leading manufacturer of building products and innovative solutions for the construction industry. USG produces Sheetrock brand drywall, Durock cement board, Securock glass-mat sheathing, and a wide range of interior finishing systems. The company serves contractors, architects, and building professionals through its distributor network and provides digital tools and APIs to support the building and construction workflow.

providers.name: Boise Cascade
providers.description: Boise Cascade is a leading North American manufacturer and distributor of building materials for the residential and commercial construction industry. The company produces engineered wood products (EWP) including I-joists, LVL beams, and glulam, as well as structural panels and lumber, and distributes a broad range of building materials through its wholesale distribution network.

providers.name: BRKZ
providers.description: BRKZ is a Saudi Arabian construction-technology company operating a B2B online marketplace for building materials and construction equipment. Positioned as a top online building materials store in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), the platform connects contractors and construction businesses with material suppliers, streamlining procurement and offering nationwide delivery across Saudi Arabia. The bilingual (Arabic and English) storefront lets buyers source construction supplies online, and the company is backed by 500 Global among its investors. This profile was enriched from BRKZ's public web presence; the company runs a private, authenticated API host (api.brkz.com) but does not publish a public developer program, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Granite Construction
providers.description: Granite Construction is one of the largest diversified heavy civil contractors and construction materials producers in the United States, with operations spanning transportation infrastructure, water infrastructure, mineral exploration, and aggregate materials.

providers.name: Hill International
providers.description: Hill International is a global construction consulting firm founded in 1976 in Mt. Laurel, New Jersey, providing program, project, and construction management, project management oversight, claims and dispute resolution, estimating and cost management, facilities management, project monitoring, troubled project turnaround, commissioning, and project labor agreement consulting to public and private sector owners across more than 100 offices in 42 countries. In December 2022 Hill agreed to be acquired by Global Infrastructure Solutions, Inc. (GISI), the parent of STV, with the take-private transaction closing in May 2023 — Hill now operates as a GISI Consulting Group company alongside STV, GEI Consultants, LiRo-Hill, Layton Construction, and the broader GISI portfolio. Hill International is a professional services firm and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or any developer portal.

providers.name: Martin Marietta Materials
providers.description: Martin Marietta Materials is a leading supplier of building materials, including aggregates, cement, ready-mixed concrete, asphalt, and paving products, used in construction, infrastructure, and residential projects across the United States.

providers.name: Planby Technologies, Inc.
providers.description: Planby Technologies, Inc. (PLANBY) is a Seoul-based AI transformation partner for architecture and construction organizations, helping construction firms, architectural offices, and interior studios adopt AI-powered workflows. Its products include PLANA (interior and concept CG rendering automation) and PLAD (apartment exterior design visualization), which cut visualization timeframes from days to hours, alongside its AX Program for organizational AI transformation (diagnosis, training, and workflow integration) and Knowledge System Building that structures construction data such as blueprints, specifications, and defect records into domain-specific data frameworks. Clients include Samsung E&A, POSCO E&C, Hyundai, Daewoo E&C, and Samsung C&T. Backed by 500 Global. PLANBY publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Plantd
providers.description: Plantd is an American advanced-materials manufacturer based in Oxford, North Carolina, founded in 2021 by former SpaceX engineers Nathan Silvernail (CEO) and Huade Tan (CTO) with Josh Dorfman (CMO). The company grows and harvests fast-growing perennial grass on farms across North Carolina and Virginia and presses it into carbon-negative structural building panels intended to replace oriented strand board (OSB), plywood and other timber-based sheathing. Production runs on a modular, all-electric, closed-loop manufacturing platform in a 150,000+ sq ft facility, with a research farm in Stovall, NC. Customers and partners include homebuilder D.R. Horton and furniture brand Studio TK. Plantd has raised roughly $47.5M across seed, Series A and a $22M Series B (October 2025). Plantd is a physical-goods manufacturer: it publishes no developer program, no public API, and no machine-readable API contract of any kind — this profile records that absence rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Toll Brothers
providers.description: Toll Brothers is the nation's leading builder of luxury homes, designing, building, marketing, and arranging financing for luxury residential communities across the United States. As a Fortune 500 company and #1 Most Admired Home Builder in Fortune magazine's 2026 list, Toll Brothers operates across 60+ markets. The company does not publicly expose developer APIs. Website integrations and home search functionality are provided through the tollbrothers.com consumer platform.

providers.name: Factory OS
providers.description: Factory OS (styled Factory_OS) is an off-site construction company founded in 2017 by Rick Holliday and Larry Pace that industrialized multifamily and affordable housing production on an assembly line inside a 275,000-square-foot facility in Building 680 on Mare Island in Vallejo, California. Union carpenters build wood-frame housing modules across roughly two dozen stations in a 33-step process, and the finished modules are trucked to the project site and assembled — an approach the company says cuts production time by about half and production cost by a quarter against conventional site-built construction. It raised roughly $132 million across three rounds, including $60 million from JPMorgan Chase and Saint-Gobain in 2021, and delivered more than 4,000 homes across California and Hawaii, about 90 percent of them affordable housing. In May 2024 the company was recapitalized and renamed Harbinger Homes (legal entity Harbinger Production Inc.), with Tom Smith as CEO and Kevin Brown as president; factoryos.com now 301-redirects every path to harbinger.homes. Harbinger filed a WARN notice on 12 February 2026 covering all 280 employees, citing a lack of new business and loss of capital funding, with layoffs beginning 13 April 2026. Factory OS is a manufacturer of physical housing modules, not a software company: it operates no developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification of any kind, and its GitHub organization has no public repositories.

providers.name: Schuettflix
providers.description: Schuettflix is a German digital logistics platform for the construction industry, founded in 2018 in Guetersloh. It operates a neutral B2B marketplace that connects construction companies, bulk-material suppliers, freight forwarders and waste-disposal firms in a single fully digital workflow. Through its iOS and Android apps, customers order sand, gravel and crushed stone with transparent real-time pricing, coordinate dispatch and transport, capture delivery documentation, manage routes, and handle mineral-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling of construction materials. The company digitizes the traditionally analog and fragmented process of procuring and delivering bulk goods, earning a commission on the transactions facilitated through its platform. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Speedinvest. No public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Schüttflix
providers.description: Schüttflix is a Gütersloh, Germany based digital logistics platform for the construction industry, describing itself as the first digital logistics hub to connect construction companies, building-material suppliers, disposal companies and carriers. The marketplace digitizes the full workflow from ordering bulk materials (sand, gravel, crushed stone) through transport dispatch to the delivery note, and adds construction-waste disposal and circular-economy recycling services. Schüttflix operates as a neutral marketplace ("we don't compete, we connect") spanning 4,000+ suppliers and disposers, 6,800+ partner carriers and 33,000+ vehicles, delivered primarily through native iOS and Android apps rather than a public API. It is a portfolio company of HV Capital, added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Riggs Distler
providers.description: Riggs Distler & Company is an energy and utility infrastructure construction firm operating since 1909. Now part of Centuri Group, the company delivers electric transmission and distribution, natural gas, renewable energy, emergency response, and heavy civil services across the United States and Canada. Riggs Distler is a field-services contractor with no public developer APIs or developer portal.

providers.name: Aikito
providers.description: Aikito is a New York-based company (founded 2021) operating a commercial real-estate platform that helps business owners design, build, finance, and manage their commercial spaces. It pairs a suite of AI-driven tools with non-dilutive financing so tenants can build out a space and pay over time, covering the project lifecycle from lease execution through move-in. Aikito was founded by Amol Sarva and its investors include Bloomberg Beta, Gaingels, Calm Ventures, FJ Labs, and Northzone. As of this profile Aikito publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or technical documentation surface, so it remains a company/identity record in the API Evangelist network rather than an API provider.

providers.name: BMC Stock Holdings
providers.description: BMC Stock Holdings, Inc. was one of the largest professional building materials distributors in the United States, serving homebuilders, remodelers, and contractors with lumber, structural components, millwork, doors, windows, and installed services. The company was formed in December 2015 through the merger of Stock Building Supply and Building Materials Holding Corporation (BMHC) and traded on NASDAQ under the ticker BMCH, headquartered in Raleigh, North Carolina. On January 1, 2021, BMC Stock Holdings completed an all-stock "merger of equals" with Builders FirstSource (NYSE: BLDR), creating the nation's largest supplier of structural building products to the professional homebuilding market. The combined company retained the Builders FirstSource name, BLDR ticker, and Irving, Texas headquarters. The merger had an enterprise value of approximately $2.5 billion and produced a company with more than $11 billion in annual sales, approximately 26,000 employees, and roughly 550 distribution and manufacturing locations across more than 40 U.S. states. BMC Stock Holdings no longer exists as an independent entity. The legacy buildwithbmc.com domain redirects to bldr.com, and BMC product lines and branches have been absorbed into the Builders FirstSource network. This profile is retained as a historical Fortune 1000 record (BMC ranked #677 prior to the merger) and as a redirect to the successor profile at api-evangelist/builders-firstsource. BMC operated as a commodity-and-services distributor and did not publish public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal. No API surface is documented for this provider.

providers.name: CalAtlantic Group
providers.description: CalAtlantic Group was a U.S. homebuilder formed on October 1, 2015 through the merger of Standard Pacific Homes and Ryland Homes. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, it became the fourth largest homebuilder in the United States before being acquired by Lennar Corporation in February 2018, which made Lennar the nation's largest homebuilder. CalAtlantic no longer operates as an independent entity and does not offer public APIs or developer resources.

providers.name: Ciridae
providers.description: Ciridae is building an AI-native operating system for services businesses — the industrial, construction, and field-service companies that make up the real economy. Its platform replaces fragmented ERPs and spreadsheets with a unified system that automates core business operations across project management, financials, CRM, accounts payable and receivable, and reporting, while keeping humans in the loop to oversee AI decisions. Modules span AI-generated field workforce scheduling, vendor onboarding and compliance, automated payment workflows, and customer order expediting, typically deployed in a two-to-four-week implementation with embedded engineers. Founded in 2025 and based in San Francisco, Ciridae is backed by Accel. The company does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Commercial Metals Company
providers.description: Commercial Metals Company (CMC) is a Fortune 500 manufacturer, recycler, and marketer of steel and metal products serving the construction, energy, and manufacturing industries. CMC was the first US steel company to launch an online customer portal (myCMC), but does not currently publish a public developer API portal or OpenAPI specifications. Programmatic integrations with myCMC (order management, shipping, invoicing) are typically established through direct contracts with CMC's IT organization rather than via a self-service developer program.

providers.name: Conjectag
providers.description: Conjectag (Conject AG / Conject Holding GmbH) was a Munich-based German construction technology company founded in 2000 that provided cloud-based software for the built environment, covering project management, collaboration, document control, and construction cost management for the AEC (architecture, engineering, and construction) sector. It was surfaced as a historical Earlybird Venture Capital portfolio company. Conject was acquired by the Australian construction collaboration platform Aconex in March 2016, and Aconex was subsequently acquired by Oracle in December 2017; the company no longer operates independently and publishes no live website or developer/API surface. This profile is retained for network provenance rather than active enrichment.

providers.name: Cover
providers.description: Cover (Cover Technologies Inc.) is a Los Angeles-based construction technology company that designs and builds custom, architect-grade backyard homes, accessory dwelling units (ADUs), and residential spaces using a prefabricated, factory-manufactured building system. Cover handles the full development process end to end, from initial consultation and design through permitting, manufacturing, and on-site installation, delivering custom spaces in weeks rather than years. The company is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. Cover is a physical-product homebuilder and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures verifiable company identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Crews By Core *
providers.description: Crews by Core was a construction field-execution platform based in Palo Alto, California (with a Tokyo office), founded and led by CEO Di-Ann Eisnor. Branded "Mission Control for the Field," its mobile-first product gave superintendents and foremen a single tool for lookahead scheduling, jobsite logistics, drawings, and field-to-office messaging, layered with AI-driven risk detection to quantify and mitigate schedule and financial risk on the jobsite. The company was backed by GV (Google Ventures) among ten investors and was acquired by construction IoT company WakeCap on July 1, 2024, folding its scheduling and communication tooling into WakeCap's worker-productivity sensor platform. Crews by Core did not expose a public developer API; this profile documents the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eggrock
providers.description: Eggrock (Eggrock Modular Solutions; legally Innovative Modular Pre-Fabrication LLC) is a North American manufacturer of prefabricated "bathroom-in-a-box" pods — complete, custom, ready-to-install bathrooms built off-site using BIM-driven design and lean manufacturing for hotels, hospitals, dormitories, military barracks, and other multi-unit construction projects. Off-site fabrication compresses construction schedules and improves quality versus building bathrooms on site. In 2012 Eggrock licensed exclusive North American manufacturing and distribution to Oldcastle Precast. It is a construction / building-products manufacturer with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable developer surface.

providers.name: Elmawkaa
providers.description: Elmawkaa (الموقع) is an Egyptian B2B online marketplace that digitizes construction-materials procurement. Founded in Cairo in 2017 by Ebrahem Anwar, Mahmoud Habib, and Mohamed Thabet, the platform lets construction companies request and compare competitive supplier quotations for materials such as cement, steel, and gypsum board, using proprietary matching algorithms to replace slow, manual bidding with a documented, automated process. A 500 Startups (500 Global) accelerator graduate that raised a seed round led by Flat6Labs with Oqal and other regional backers, Elmawkaa was fully acquired by Saudi PropTech / real-estate-appraisal platform Ayen in a seven-figure deal in October 2024, with its marketplace folded into Ayen's services. Elmawkaa publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation, and its standalone domain (elmawkaa.com) no longer resolves following the acquisition.

providers.name: Fastenal
providers.description: Fastenal is a leading distributor of industrial and construction supplies, offering fasteners, tools, safety equipment, and other industrial products through stores, vending, and e-commerce. While Fastenal provides EDI integrations and supply chain programs like FAST 360, FASTBin, and FASTStock to enterprise customers, no publicly documented API specifications are available.

providers.name: Getable
providers.description: Getable is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Historically Getable operated a construction and equipment rental marketplace/software platform (getable.com). As of this enrichment pass the original company appears inactive; the getable.com domain resolves to a general home-services and equipment-rental lead-generation marketplace with no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or other public API surface. No OpenAPI, MCP, or agent-facing artifacts could be sourced, so this profile remains an identity stub rather than a scored API provider.

providers.name: Illinois Tool Works
providers.description: Illinois Tool Works (ITW) is a Fortune 500 global multi-industrial manufacturer of value-added consumables and specialty equipment with related service businesses across automotive OEM, food equipment, test and measurement, electronics, welding, polymers and fluids, construction products, and specialty products. ITW does not publish a public API or developer program. This repository exists to track APIs, SDKs, and developer resources should they become available.

providers.name: Infra.Market
providers.description: Infra.Market is a technology-enabled building materials platform serving India's construction and real estate sectors across the entire project lifecycle. Operating as a house of brands, it supplies concrete, aggregates, steel, AAC blocks, plywood, tiles, sanitaryware, paints, plumbing, modular kitchens, hardware, electricals, appliances, and rental equipment through both B2B (direct corporate sales with site delivery) and B2R (retail via dealers and distributors across 17,000+ touchpoints). It is backed by 280+ manufacturing facilities across 22 Indian states under brands including Shalimar Paints, RDC, IVAS, Robo, and Ultrafine, and is headquartered in Thane, Maharashtra. Added to the API Evangelist network as an Accel portfolio company; no public developer API surface has been identified to date.

providers.name: Kanler
providers.description: Kanler was a Redwood City, California home-improvement marketplace and construction technology company that connected homeowners with vetted home-improvement professionals and managed their projects end to end, positioning itself around price transparency and project peace of mind. Seed-funded in 2016 with backing from Battery Ventures, Floodgate Fund, TriplePoint Capital and Flight VC, the company later operated as a custom-home and whole-house remodeling firm. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass its primary domain (kanler.com) returns HTTP 404 and no public developer, API, or documentation surface could be found, so no API artifacts were produced.

providers.name: Katerra
providers.description: Katerra was a Menlo Park, California off-site construction and building-technology company founded in 2015 by former Flextronics chief executive Michael Marks with Fritz Wolff and Jim Davidson, built on the thesis that a single vertically integrated firm could design, engineer, manufacture and assemble buildings end to end — running its own architecture practice, factories in Phoenix, Tracy and Spokane producing cross-laminated timber and prefabricated wall, floor and bathroom assemblies, and its own supply chain and general contracting arm. It raised more than $2 billion across a dozen rounds, including an $865M Series D led by the SoftBank Vision Fund in January 2018 at a valuation above $3 billion and a $200M recapitalization in December 2020 that handed SoftBank majority control. Its only software product was Katerra Apollo, announced in February 2019 as a design-to-field platform (Apollo Construct, Apollo Insight, Apollo Connect) whose launch materials promised "open API integration" with existing construction workflows — but Apollo was sold to Katerra's own construction customers and never shipped a public developer portal, API reference, SDK or machine-readable specification. The insolvency of its SoftBank-backed lender Greensill Capital cost Katerra its bonding capacity, and the company shut down and filed Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas on 6 June 2021. Its assets were broken up: the Apollo software went to Builders FirstSource for roughly $4.5M on 9 September 2021, and the factories were sold separately. katerra.com no longer serves a site — it answers a Cloudflare error 1001 on every path and cannot complete a TLS handshake at all. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface left to catalog.

providers.name: KB Home
providers.description: KB Home is one of the largest and most recognized homebuilders in the United States, building single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums for first-time, move-up, and active adult buyers across more than 45 markets.

providers.name: Libra Robotics
providers.description: Libra Robotics is a Silicon Valley robotics startup building autonomous robots that install solar panels in the field, targeting projects from 1 MW upward across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, and agrivoltaic applications. The company's field system — marketed as Libra 001 — combines purpose-built end-effectors, suction-based panel handling and transport, vision and positioning systems that align each module with the tracker structure, and fastener workflows compatible with multiple commercial racking systems, operating across day and night shifts. Libra Robotics was founded by Yaojing Huang and Jermaine Zhao, is part of the Y Combinator Summer 2026 batch, and operates out of Newark, California. As of this profile the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable specifications; its web presence is a six-page marketing site covering solutions, technology, safety, company, and contact.

providers.name: Lumina
providers.description: Lumina (Lumina Innovations) is a San Francisco-based startup building all-electric, autonomous heavy construction equipment. Founded by Ahmed Shubber and Federico Di Palma, the company develops both the hardware and the self-driving software in-house, taking a Tesla/Waymo-style approach to the excavation and earth-moving industry. Its flagship Moonlander ML6 is a 32-ton fully autonomous electric bulldozer with roughly 750 horsepower of peak output and a 414 kWh battery pack. The broader product lineup spans Roadrunner, Moonlander, Bladerunner, and a Powerpack energy system. Lumina does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Manitowoc
providers.description: Manitowoc Cranes is one of the world's largest providers of lifting equipment for the global construction industry, including lattice-boom crawler cranes, tower cranes, mobile hydraulic cranes, and boom trucks. No public developer APIs have been documented.

providers.name: meetdavis
providers.description: Davis (meetdavis.com) is an AI-native real estate technology company, backed by Heartcore Capital and Balderton Capital, that compresses early-stage real estate development from months to days. Davis combines proprietary AI models with human architect expertise to deliver feasibility studies (site analysis, regulatory diagnostics, volumetrics, financial modeling) and architectural designs (floor plans, unit-mix optimization, space planning) directly to developers and investors. Its first proprietary model, Gaudi-1, performs automated architectural generation under regulatory and financial constraints. Davis operates as a service model rather than selling software, and publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs at this time. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from the Balderton Capital portfolio and has been through the enrichment pipeline; no API surface was found.

providers.name: Module
providers.description: Module is a vertically integrated sustainable housing company that designs, manufactures, and builds modular homes. Operating across design (architecture and engineering with BIM), manufacturing (its Last Mile Facility in Pittsburgh), and construction (licensed general contracting), Module focuses on infill and "missing middle" housing, small-footprint and energy-efficient affordable homes, and mixed-income developments through its Last Mile Network of design, construction, and mission-driven developer partner programs. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched in the API Evangelist network; Module publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation surface.

providers.name: Mosaic Building Group
providers.description: Mosaic (Mosaic Building Group) is a full-stack construction technology company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. It is a national leader in build-to-rent residential construction and pre-development, pairing in-house software with local homebuilding partners to deliver personalized homes faster and at lower cost across Arizona and Texas. Its Mosaic Hub platform applies AI to construction planning and operations management. Backed by a16z (Series A lead) alongside Greylock, Innovation Endeavors, Founders Fund, Thrive Capital, SV Angel, and 8VC. Mosaic operates as a hybrid construction-plus-software business and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Plan0 Ai
providers.description: Plan0 AI is a real estate construction technology company that applies AI to preconstruction cost estimation and design analysis. Its platform turns architectural drawings into detailed cost estimates and 3D models in roughly 30 minutes rather than the traditional two-week cycle, and adds automated takeoff and pricing, value-engineering scenario simulation, and predictive analytics. Plan0 AI serves real estate developers underwriting and making preconstruction design decisions, general contractors producing business- development estimates and cost forecasts, and investors validating pro-formas and benchmarking. Surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing and demo-booking website only, with no public API, developer documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Plant Prefab
providers.description: Plant Prefab is a Southern California offsite construction technology company that custom-fabricates panelized and modular building components to deliver housing and hospitality projects in roughly half the time of traditional site-built construction. Its panel-based building system spans open-cavity panels to fully finished modules, and its LivingHomes product line and in-house Plant Design Studio offer customized, sustainable designs recognized with LEED Platinum, NAHB Energy Value Housing, and AIA Top Ten Green Projects awards. The company is backed by Obvious Ventures and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Powerplay
providers.description: Powerplay is a construction project management platform built by Coffer Internet Services Pvt. Ltd. (Bengaluru, India) that gives builders, general contractors, subcontractors, project managers, and site engineers mobile and desktop tools to run construction projects end to end: real-time work and progress tracking, material procurement and inventory management, labor attendance and payroll, issue tracking, petty-cash and expense management, and reporting dashboards. The product is delivered primarily through iOS and Android field apps with a desktop companion. Powerplay does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation, so this profile captures its identity and web surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Primavera Systems
providers.description: Primavera Systems, Inc. was a project-management and project-portfolio-management software company best known for the Primavera P6 scheduling platform used in construction, engineering, and capital-projects industries. It was acquired by Oracle Corporation in 2008 and folded into Oracle's Construction and Engineering business, where the products live on as Oracle Primavera. As an independent company it no longer exists, its primavera.com domain now redirects to oracle.com/primavera, and it publishes no independent public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation of its own. This profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead, but that association does not match the acquired-by-Oracle entity and appears to be a name-matching artifact.

providers.description: PulteGroup is one of America's largest homebuilding companies, building homes under the Centex, Pulte Homes, Del Webb, DiVosta Homes, John Wieland Homes, and American West brands. No public developer APIs have been identified at this time; this index tracks the company's public web properties.

providers.name: Renotag, Inc.
providers.description: Renotag, Inc. is a Calgary, Canada based construction-technology startup (founded 2020, backed by 500 Global) that builds home-renovation and construction cost-estimation software. Its product produces localized renovation estimates and material takeoffs in minutes by combining user inputs with regional labor and material pricing data, helping contractors quote and close more business. As of this enrichment pass Renotag publishes no public developer program, API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documentation surface; the primary web properties (renotag.com and api.renotag.com) currently return HTTP 301 redirect loops, and the app is a private login at app.renotag.com. This profile is retained as a portfolio lead surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio.

providers.name: Revolution Precrafted
providers.description: Revolution Precrafted is a Manila, Philippines-based prefabricated design and proptech company founded in 2015 by Robbie Antonio. It designs and sells limited-edition prefab homes, pavilions, modular hotels, pop-up retail spaces, glamping structures, and furniture created by more than 80 leading global architects, designers, and artists under exclusive partnership. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Durians) and K2 Global, it reached a reported unicorn valuation. The company runs a consumer real-estate and construction business and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or technical documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and mislabeled "Strategic Grow" in the source stub; the website revolutionprecrafted.com is authoritative.

providers.name: Rudus
providers.description: Rudus is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) startup building an AI-powered takeoff and estimation platform for concrete contractors and subcontractors. The software automatically detects and classifies concrete structures (footings, walls, columns, and slabs) from architectural plan sets, expands them into detailed assembly line items, and integrates into existing estimator workflows rather than replacing them. Rudus reports a 70-80% reduction in takeoff and estimation time, letting estimators submit more bids. Founded by Rishi Pankhaniya (ex-Airbnb) and Sahil Goel (ex-Amazon). As of this enrichment pass Rudus operates a lead-generation marketing site at rudus.ai with no public developer program, API, documentation, or self-service sign-up; this profile records that verified state.

providers.name: Samara
providers.description: Samara is a residential design and construction company that builds prefabricated, factory-made homes. Founded as an independent venture by Airbnb co-founder Joe Gebbia, Samara designs and delivers backyard accessory dwelling units (ADUs) in configurable Studio, One Bedroom, Two Bedroom, XL 8 and XL 10 models, alongside "Locale by Samara" single-family homes and a modular "kit of parts" for higher-yield multifamily infill. The company pairs a consumer-facing online configurator, property-eligibility checks, financing options and regional showrooms with factory production and installation. Backed by General Catalyst, Samara operates in the housing, construction technology and real-estate space. It is a physical-product company with no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Smart Reno
providers.description: Smart Reno is a Montreal-based home-renovation marketplace, founded in 2012 by Andrei Uglar, that connects homeowners with qualified, available local contractors. Homeowners post a project and receive up to three competing quotes from vetted renovation professionals through a proprietary contractor-matching platform. Backed by 500 Startups (500 Global), Anges Quebec, and BDC, Smart Reno was acquired by RBC Ventures in 2019 and now operates its consumer marketplace under the soumissionrenovation.ca brand across Quebec, Ontario, and Alberta. The company exposes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or webhook surface; smartreno.com 301-redirects to the successor site and no /.well-known discovery documents were found.

providers.name: StructionSite
providers.description: StructionSite was a construction-technology company providing jobsite reality-capture and progress-documentation software (360-degree walkthrough video and photo documentation of construction sites, tied to project plans). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the standalone StructionSite brand has been absorbed by its acquirer DroneDeploy - structionsite.com, www.structionsite.com, and api.structionsite.com all HTTP 301-redirect to www.dronedeploy.com. No independent StructionSite developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, package, or /.well-known discovery surface could be found; any API surface now lives under the DroneDeploy brand.

providers.name: The Boring Company
providers.description: The Boring Company is an American infrastructure and tunnel-construction company founded by Elon Musk in 2016 that designs and builds underground transportation, utility, and freight tunnels to reduce urban traffic congestion. Its Prufrock tunnel-boring machines dig low-cost tunnels roughly a mile a week, and its all-electric, zero-emissions Loop system carries passengers in Tesla vehicles through those tunnels — the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop is its first commercial deployment. The company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs; its web presence is marketing, careers, Vegas Loop ticketing, and a merchandise store.

providers.name: Advanced Drainage Systems
providers.description: Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS) is a leading manufacturer of stormwater and onsite septic wastewater solutions. The company produces drainage infrastructure including pipes, chambers, basins, and water quality treatment products serving residential, commercial, agricultural, airport, and transportation markets. ADS provides CAD integrations and engineering resources for civil engineering professionals.

providers.name: Hosta a.i.
providers.description: Hosta a.i. is an AI-powered remote property assessment platform that turns ordinary photographs from any camera into precise measurements, detailed floor plans, material classifications, condition assessments, and bills of materials. Using patented AI spatial and material analytics, Hosta automates onsite property analysis without specialized equipment or site visits, and exposes these capabilities through configurable APIs so insurers, appraisers, inspectors, contractors, property managers, home-improvement platforms, and furniture retailers can embed remote assessment into their existing workflows and systems. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, Hosta is a Techstars- and Eclipse-backed company operating on a secure AWS cloud platform with PII filtering protections.

providers.name: Green Canopy NODE
providers.description: Green Canopy NODE is a Seattle- and Portland-based sustainable real estate development and construction technology company that designs and builds all-electric, low-carbon homes. The business operates across three lines: prefabricated "Building Kits" (including mass-timber panelized systems), full development services for multi-unit and infill housing projects, and impact investment funds that finance green housing. The company reports 300+ all-electric homes built, five real estate investment funds, and roughly 35K metric tons of greenhouse-gas emissions mitigated since inception. Green Canopy NODE was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. It publishes a marketing and investor website but no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API surface at this time.

providers.name: Builders FirstSource
providers.description: Builders FirstSource (NYSE: BLDR) is the nation's largest supplier and manufacturer of structural building products, value-added components, and construction services to the professional market for single-family and multi-family construction. The company operates approximately 570 locations across 43 states with 28,000 team members, headquartered in Irving, Texas. Its product portfolio includes lumber, manufactured components, doors, windows, millwork, cabinets, and roofing, complemented by digital procurement and project management tools through the myBLDR platform.

providers.name: Doxel
providers.description: Doxel is a Menlo Park, California construction technology company providing AI-powered observability and progress tracking for large capital projects. Founded in 2015 by CEO Saurabh Ladha, the company combines 360-degree reality capture (via Insta360 X5 hardware partnership) with computer vision models that compare site video against BIM models to automatically quantify work-in-place by trade, system, and stage. The platform layers a "rules of credit" engine on top of those quantities to drive earned-value, schedule, and budget analytics — including 3D Progress View, Production Rates, Schedule (a visual Gantt replacement), Utilities Underground Tracking from drone imagery, and Portfolio-level dashboards. Doxel uses advanced language models to map schedule line items to physical progress and supports Procore-style construction management workflows, with deployments across data centers, healthcare, semiconductor fabs, and EV battery factories. Doxel has raised approximately $57M from Insight Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, and others, and counts 18 of the top 30 U.S. general contractors, 14 of the top 20 data center developers, and 3 of 4 hyperscalers as customers. There is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, or GitHub organization — the platform is delivered as a managed SaaS application at app.doxel.ai with hardware-assisted capture and enterprise integrations arranged via direct engagement.

providers.name: Prescient
providers.description: Prescient Co. Inc. was a United States construction-technology and manufacturing company that sold an integrated design, engineering, manufacturing and assembly platform for multi-unit buildings — apartments, condominiums, student and military dormitories, hotels and senior-living communities. Its product was the patented Prescient Solution built on the Unified Truss Construction System (UTCS), a light-gauge steel structural framing system manufactured off-site in panelised components and assembled on-site, marketed as a faster, greener and lower-cost alternative to conventional cast-in-place and wood-frame structures at heights up to roughly twelve stories. The "technology" in the offering was internal design-automation software that linked architectural design, structural engineering, factory manufacturing and field assembly into one digital model; it was delivered as a design-build service to real-estate developers and general contractors, never as a product a third party could integrate with. Founded in 2012 (some sources list 2013) and headquartered in North Carolina — Charlotte, later Durham — with manufacturing in Mebane, North Carolina and Arvada, Colorado, the company raised a large private round stack including a $40M Series D and a Series E led by Eldridge Industries at a reported $650M valuation; publicly reported lifetime totals disagree, with EquityZen listing $103M and Crunchbase reporting roughly $375M through Series G. The company contracted sharply: the Mebane plant closed in 2022 with 83 jobs cut, 50 Arvada jobs were cut in April 2023, and a Colorado WARN notice filed on 31 August 2023 announced the permanent closure of the Arvada plant and a further 60 jobs, stating that upon conclusion of the shutdown activities the company would be closed. Prescient never operated a public developer program, API, SDK, webhook surface or machine-readable specification, and prescientco.com has since passed out of the company's control. This profile is retained as a historical record; there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Duane Morris
providers.description: Duane Morris LLP is a Philadelphia-headquartered, full-service U.S. and international law firm founded in 1904 by Russell Duane, Steven Heckscher, and Roland S. Morris. Chaired by Matthew A. Taylor, the firm describes itself as "a law firm with more than 900 attorneys in offices across the United States and internationally" — with a U.S. footprint spanning the East Coast, Texas, the Mountain West, and California, plus international offices in London, Singapore, Vietnam (Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City), Shanghai, Myanmar, and joint ventures/alliances reaching Mexico and Latin America. An Am Law 100 firm since 2001, Duane Morris is known for depth in intellectual property (including patent prosecution and PTAB practice), trial and appellate litigation, real estate, corporate transactions, employment, healthcare, cannabis, and life sciences. The firm publishes an extensive LexBlog-powered thought-leadership network of more than 50 practice-area blogs, all of which expose RSS 2.0 feeds via the standard WordPress /feed/ convention. Duane Morris does not expose any public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI spec, GraphQL endpoint, webhooks, status page, or developer portal; the GitHub organization github.com/duanemorris exists but has no public repositories. The firm's only machine-readable surfaces are the RSS feeds of its blog network.

providers.name: Cosmic Robotics
providers.description: Cosmic Robotics, Inc. designs and operates autonomous construction equipment that takes on the hardest, most dangerous jobs on a construction site, coordinated as a fleet by a single software layer. The flagship Cosmic-1A is a purpose-built robotic platform for solar panel installation, and Constellation is the coordination and control layer that plans, dispatches, and monitors the robot fleet across a jobsite. Founded in 2023 and based in the Dogpatch neighborhood of San Francisco, the company is backed by Y Combinator. providers.name: Day & Zimmermann
providers.description: Day & Zimmermann is a privately held, family-owned diversified industrial services company founded in 1901 and headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Yoh family has controlled the company since 1961; Harold L. Yoh III serves as Chairman and CEO. Day & Zimmermann reported approximately $2.7 billion in revenue in 2023 with roughly 43,000–52,000 employees across approximately 150 global locations.
